summary: An ode in which three urn-like figures, Love, Ambition and Poesy, drift past the indolent speaker who bids them farewell to keep his blissful idleness. It treats indolence, the artist's vocation, ambition, and the Grecian urn.

title: ODE ON MELANCHOLY
author: Keats
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Ode arguing that melancholy dwells within beauty and joy themselves, to be embraced rather than drugged away; the inseparability of joy and grief, beauty, transience and mortality.

title: ODE TO A NIGHTINGALE
author: Keats
summary: Great ode in which the bird's deathless song draws the poet toward easeful death and the imagination, then back to his sole self; mortality, transience, the immortality of art and the longing to escape human suffering.

title: Ode to Apollo
author: Keats
summary: An ode imagining Apollo's western halls where the great bards (Homer, Virgil, Milton, Shakespeare, Spenser, Tasso) sing in turn; the poet's pantheon, music and song, classical myth.

title: Ode to Fanny
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: An ode begging Fanny to keep her heart's pulse for the speaker alone, racked by jealousy and treating love as a sacred religion. Its themes are romantic love, jealousy, and love as worship.

title: ODE TO GEORGIANA, DUCHESS OF DEVONSHIRE
author: Coleridge
summary: A Pindaric ode praising the Duchess for hailing Tell's freedom despite her privileged birth, contrasting aristocratic luxury with the toiler's misery and celebrating maternal love and social liberty.

title: ODE TO PSYCHE
author: Keats
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Ode building a shrine to the late-born goddess Psyche within the poet's own mind; classical myth, love (Cupid and Psyche), and the imagination as the true temple of the divine.

title: ODE TO THE DEPARTING YEAR
author: Coleridge
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A Pindaric ode lamenting the bloodshed of 1796, prophesying divine judgement on warring tyrants and on England; themes of providence, war's cost and patriotic dread for Albion.

title: ODE TO TRANQUILLITY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: An ode invoking Tranquillity above Fame, contrasting calm contemplative nature with the feverish, blood-and-guile 'trade' of present men, a retreat into philosophic peace.

title: OF BALIOL COLLEGE, OXFORD, AUTHOR OF THE ‘RETROSPECT’, AND OTHER POEMS
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet to Southey whose melodies wake memory and hope; dwells on the bittersweet pleasure of recollected past delight; themes of memory, friendship, and poetry.

title: Of Him I Love Day and Night
author: Whitman
summary: Dream of searching burial-places for a dead beloved and finding every place full of the dead; resolves to dispense with graves, content with death everywhere.

title: OF HUMANE LEARNING
author: Coleridge
summary: Stanza from Fulke Greville used by Coleridge as a motto on learning and faith, arguing that true understanding lives only where knowledge breeds obedience and works.

title: Of That Blithe Throat of Thine
author: Whitman
summary: The poet takes the arctic bird's gay song as a lesson, singing cheerfully even amid the winter of old age.

title: Of the Awefull Battle of the Pekes and the Pollicles
author: Eliot
summary: Mock-heroic comic battle of dogs broken up by the Great Rumpuscat; light verse parodying tribal warfare among pets.

title: Of the Terrible Doubt of Appearances
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Philosophical Calamus poem where epistemological doubt (appearance vs reality, identity beyond the grave) is answered not by reason but by the touch of the beloved comrade.

title: Oh, I am frighten’d with most hateful thoughts!
author: Keats
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A fragment in which the lover frets that his idealized beloved may have ordinary flaws, comparing her to Dian and Juno. It treats romantic idealization, doubt, and appearance versus reality.

title: Old Age’s Lambent Peaks
author: Whitman
summary: A late valedictory lyric celebrating the elevated, illuminating vista of old age at life's golden twilight, where calmer perspective reveals the best of experience.

title: Old Age’s Ship & Crafty Death’s
author: Whitman
summary: Old age and death imagined as rival vessels closing in, met with defiant joy of strife as the poet's ship crowds on full sail toward the open sea.

title: Old Chants
author: Whitman
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A roll-call of the world's ancient poets and epics from Egypt, the Bible, Greece, and medieval legend, acknowledging America's debt to old poems and traditions.

title: Old Deuteronomy
author: Eliot
summary: Comic verse on the ancient village cat who has lived many lives in succession and is revered by all; gently touches age and the nine lives.

title: Old Ireland
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Allegory of Ireland as a grieving ancient mother over an empty grave, consoled that her dead son lives risen in a new country; grief, resurrection, exile, and rebirth in America.

title: OLD POSSUM’S BOOK  OF PRACTICAL CATS
author: Eliot
summary: Collection header for Eliot's light comic verse about cats; opens with The Naming of Cats on the inscrutable third name each cat keeps secret.

title: Old Salt Kossabone
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative of an old sailor ancestor who dies at his window the moment he sees a ship win free to the open sea.

title: Old War-Dreams
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A free-verse lyric with refrain recounting recurring nightmares of the Civil War dead; themes of war's cost, dreams, memory and death.

title: The Old Song
author: Chesterton
summary: An apocalyptic ballad of London Bridge broken down, the kings who 'buy and sell', and Cobbett as the Horseman of Apocalypse; a populist, anti-plutocratic vision of England renewed.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's 'Parish Boy's Progress' tracing an orphan from the workhouse into Fagin's London criminal underworld; central themes are poverty, the cruelty of the Poor Law, the corruption of innocence by a criminal world, and the survival of inborn goodness.

title: On
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A collection of Belloc's familiar 'On ...' essays ranging over travel, letters, controversy, climate and the modern world, mixing whimsy with satire. Pieces such as 'On an Educational Reform' propose teaching Fraud as the master subject of modern commercial success, skewering the money-getting ethos of the age.

title: ON A CATARACT FROM A CAVERN NEAR THE SUMMIT OF A MOUNTAIN PRECIPICE: STROPHE
author: Coleridge
summary: An ode-strophe personifying a mountain waterfall as an 'unperishing youth' born of hidden nature, a sublime hymn to ceaseless natural renewal and mystery.

title: ON A DISCOVERY MADE TOO LATE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Sonnet probing the bleeding heart wounded by jealousy and lost hope; grief, jealousy, madness, and the painful self-reproach of reason. Form: sonnet.

title: ON A LADY WEEPING
author: Coleridge
summary: A delicate imitation from the Latin describing the tears on a lady's cheek as gems in which Love bathes his wings, blending tender pathos with playful conceit.

title: ON A LATE CONNUBIAL RUPTURE IN HIGH LIFE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet sympathizing with the wronged Princess of Wales amid the pomp of state, and her infant; themes of unhappy marriage, grief, and the hollowness of rank.

title: ON A LATE MARRIAGE BETWEEN AN OLD MAID AND FRENCH PETIT MAÎTRE
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram mocking a foolish marriage, playing on the proverb of leading apes in hell.

title: On a Portrait
author: Eliot
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Sonnet on a painted woman who stands beyond the reach of the viewer's thought — an evanescent, lamia-like enigma watched by a silent parrot; mystery, the unattainable, the inscrutable feminine.

title: ON A READER OF HIS OWN VERSES
author: Coleridge
summary: A literary-satirical epigram (after Wernicke) mocking 'Mævius', a vain bad poet who reads his hobbling verse to all, 'an ass without an ear.'

title: ON A REPORT OF A MINISTER’S DEATH
author: Coleridge
summary: A political-satirical epigram (after Lessing) on a city's hollow grief at the false report of a minister's death.

title: ON A RUINED HOUSE IN A ROMANTIC COUNTRY
author: Coleridge
summary: A mock-Gothic sonnet burlesquing the picturesque ruin and the nursery-rhyme 'House that Jack Built', parodying sentimental and Gothic verse conventions; satire in sonnet form with the ruin and moon motifs.

title: ON A SLANDERER
author: Coleridge
summary: A grotesque mock-epitaph epigram on a slanderer ('Backbite') buried in haste, whose grave gives off a mephitic stench.

title: ON A VOLUNTEER SINGER
author: Coleridge
summary: A two-line satirical epigram wishing certain bad singers would die before they sing, punning on the swan-song topos.

title: On Abolishing Sunday
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An essay defending the universal human need for a sabbath rhythm against Bolshevist abolition; critique of dehumanised progressive ideology and the rhythm of creation.

title: On Abraham Lincoln
author: Chesterton
summary: A paradox-driven essay celebrating Lincoln as a 'failure who happened to succeed', a thinker and near-martyr at odds with his success-worshipping admirers.

title: On America
author: Chesterton
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: An essay on the American Civil War as a clash of civilizations, mourning the destroyed culture of the Old South and the lost spirit of Honour.

title: ON AN AMOROUS DOCTOR
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram on a lovesick physician (Sangrado) struck by Cupid's dart, plus a jab at fashionable Bristol atheists.

title: ON AN INFANT WHICH DIED BEFORE BAPTISM
author: Coleridge
summary: An epigrammatic epitaph consoling that an unbaptized infant, dying at the mother's breast, is a 'Possessor, not Inheritor' of the kingdom of the Blest.

title: ON AN INSIGNIFICANT
author: Coleridge
summary: Mock-epitaph epigrams (after Lessing) on a nonentity ('Cypher') reduced to dust and a miser ('Avaro') whose soul rots in the grave.

title: On Anything
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A collection of Belloc's familiar essays and sketches ranging over travel in France and Spain, the writing of history, poets and prophets, and whimsical fables. The prevailing temper is nostalgic, anti-modern and rooted in landscape, memory and the pleasures of the road.

title: ON BALA HILL
author: Coleridge
summary: Sonnet of climbing a hill and reading the journeyed plain as an emblem of life's tedious way toward a hoped-for home; autumn, mutability, hope.

title: On Darwinism and Mystery
author: Chesterton
summary: An essay arguing that science is now doubting itself, that Darwinism is logically inconsistent, and that what remains is an unfathomable mystery he believes divine; faith, doubt, and the limits of reason.

title: On Death
author: Keats
summary: A short meditative lyric likening death to sleep and life to a dream, questioning why men cling to a life of woe; its central matter is mortality and the transience of earthly pleasure.

title: ON DEPUTY ——
author: Coleridge
summary: A self-referential epigram swearing off epigrams against fools, plus a political pun on a French-style 'direc-tory' governing Britain.

title: ON DONNE’S POEM ‘TO A FLEA
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty squib ennobling fleas immortalised by Donne, plus an ex-libris jingle and the famous burlesque ode on Fichte's idealism ('I, I, I! I itself I!'); literary allusion, philosophical parody, and immortality through verse.

title: On Everything
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A gathering of Belloc's familiar essays, most first printed in the Morning Post, ranging over song, travel through western England, rivers, old towns, rest and death. The reflective, digressive voice celebrates ordinary rooted life, the common man and the English countryside against the encroachments of a hurried modern age.

title: On Evil Euphemisms
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A satirical essay attacking the modern habit of disguising vices ('Companionate Marriage', 'Free Love', 'Birth-Control') under flattering euphemisms; truth, deception, and the falsity of the age.

title: ON FIRST LOOKING INTO CHAPMAN’S HOMER
author: Keats
summary: Petrarchan sonnet figuring the discovery of Homer through Chapman as an astronomer's or explorer's awe; the sublime of reading, wonder and literary discovery.

title: ON IMITATION
author: Coleridge
summary: An epigram on the ease of imitating vice and folly versus the difficulty of imitating wisdom, satirizing the gaming and drinking of would-be Foxes and Pitts.

title: On Journeys Through the States
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Poet as wandering teacher-lover traveling the States and the world like the returning seasons; the open road, America, eternal return.

title: ON LEAVING SOME FRIENDS AT AN EARLY HOUR
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Sonnet of ecstatic poetic aspiration amid visionary celestial imagery, reluctant to leave friends and be alone; friendship, imagination and the poet's striving.

title: On Lying In Bed
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A whimsical essay defending idle lying in bed, attacking the modern strengthening of minor morals at the expense of major ones; paradox, humility, and the heroic virtues.

title: ON MR. ROSS, USUALLY COGNOMINATED NOSY
author: Coleridge
summary: A cluster of epigrams (after Lessing) on a big-nosed man, on avoiding marriage, and on a liar who deceives only by telling the truth.

title: ON MY JOYFUL DEPARTURE FROM THE SAME CITY
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic epigram companion-piece, joyfully leaving the 'body-and-soul-stinking town of Cologne', wine and a church the only redeeming things. Themes: satire, the city, comedy.

title: On Nothing and Kindred Subjects
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A collection of Belloc's familiar essays, opening with a mock-metaphysical dedication praising Nothing as the stuff the world was made of. The pieces range over inns, railways, tea, lost manuscripts, death and the pleasure of taking up one's pen, blending whimsy, paradox and reflection.

title: ON OBSERVING A BLOSSOM ON THE FIRST OF FEBRUARY 1796
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric on a too-early blossom doomed by winter, likened to a consumptive girl, to Chatterton, and to Poland's killed hope; themes of transience, mortality, and the fragility of hope.

title: On Oxford A Parody
author: Keats
summary: A light parody of Wordsworth describing Oxford's Gothic decay, bishops, deer and gluttonous parsons; comic satire of place and clerical society.

title: ON PITT AND FOX
author: Coleridge
summary: Political epigrams on the deaths of statesmen Pitt and Fox, sardonically praising the dead, plus an adage that of the dead one says only good; satire of politics and the convention of speaking well of the dead.

title: ON RECEIVING A CURIOUS SHELL, AND A COPY OF VERSES, FROM THE SAME LADIES
author: Keats
summary: Playful occasional poem casting a gift-exchange as chivalric fairy romance (Armida, Rinaldo, Oberon, Titania); friendship and fancy in a medieval-fairy key.

title: On Receiving a Laurel Crown from Leigh Hunt
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet on the burden and ambition of the laurel crown given by Leigh Hunt, the poet straining for an immortal thought while time flies; poetic vocation and fame.

title: ON RECEIVING AN ACCOUNT THAT HIS ONLY SISTER’S DEATH WAS INEVITABLE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A grief-stricken sonnet anticipating the death of the poet's sister so soon after a brother's, expressing the desolation of bereavement and a longing for death rather than a loveless life.

title: ON REVISITING THE SEA-SHORE AFTER LONG ABSENCE, UNDER STRONG MEDICAL RECOMMENDATION NOT TO BATHE
author: Coleridge
summary: A joyful lyric greeting the ocean after long absence, defying the physician's warning of death and affirming health, hope, divine indwelling and the deathlessness of love.

title: ON SEEING A YOUTH AFFECTIONATELY WELCOMED BY A SISTER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A sonnet of mourning recalling the poet's dead sister's gentle virtues, prompted by the sight of another youth's sisterly welcome, finding bitter comfort that for her the grave is peace.

title: On Seeing the Elgin Marbles
author: Keats
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A sonnet on the dizzy pain of mortality felt before the Greek marbles, mingling grandeur with the wasting of time; mortality, the sublime, Grecian art and the ravages of time.

title: ON SIR RUBICUND NASO
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram (after Lessing) on a red-nosed court alderman and gossip, punning that all his talk is 'under the rose.'

title: On Something
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A collection of Belloc's familiar essays and sketches (reprinted from the Westminster Gazette, Clarion and others), ranging from a mock plea for a 'simpler drama' in blank verse to meditations on notebooks, bridges, immortality, sacramental things, and the empire-builder. The pieces mix whimsy, satire of modern life, and Catholic reflection on permanence and the ordinary man.

title: On the Beach at Night
author: Whitman
summary: A father comforts his weeping child as burial-clouds devour the stars, promising something more immortal than the stars; free-verse lyric on night, stars, mortality and immortality.

title: On the Beach at Night Alone
author: Whitman
summary: Alone by the night sea the poet perceives a vast similitude interlocking all things, times and beings; free-verse meditative lyric on the sea, stars, cosmic unity and the soul.

title: ON THE CHRISTENING OF A FRIEND’S CHILD
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A baptismal lyric blessing a friend's child, wishing her the virtues of her mother and closing with a rose emblem of generational renewal; themes of childhood, faith and time.

title: ON THE CURIOUS CIRCUMSTANCE
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty Wernicke-derived epigram on the gendering of sun and moon in English vs German, ending in a bawdy joke about cuckolded husbands; satire of marriage and gender.

title: ON THE GRASSHOPPER AND CRICKET
author: Keats
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Sonnet on 'the poetry of earth' that never dies, the grasshopper in summer and cricket in winter; nature, the seasons and the perpetuity of natural song.

title: ON THE PROSPECT OF ESTABLISHING A PANTISOCRACY IN AMERICA
author: Coleridge
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Sonnet contrasting old-world anxiety, despotism and war with the hope of bliss and equality on a transatlantic shore; reform, liberty, utopian emigration.

title: ON THE SICKNESS OF A GREAT MINISTER
author: Coleridge
summary: A political-satirical epigram (after Lessing) in which Pluto and Death spare an ailing minister ('Billy'/Pitt), mocking ministers and quacks.

title: On, on the Same, Ye Jocund Twain!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A self-summing chant of the poet's life and recitative carried into old age, fusing personal soul with the democratic destiny of America and humanity.

title: Once I Pass’d Through a Populous City
author: Whitman
summary: Of a whole city only a clinging lover is remembered; love, memory, the city, parting. Short free-verse lyric.

title: One Hour to Madness and Joy
author: Whitman
summary: Ecstatic outburst of erotic abandon and freedom, a return to Paradise in one hour of fullness; lust, joy, madness, paradise. Free verse.

title: The Advantages of having One Leg
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An essay on finding gratitude and wonder in limitation, drawn from a sprained foot; the optimism hidden in all surrender, isolating a thing to enjoy it perfectly.

title: One’s-Self I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Programmatic opening lyric of Leaves of Grass balancing the single self against the democratic en-masse, celebrating body and soul, male and female equally; free-verse manifesto.

title: Orange Buds by Mail from Florida
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Orange buds mailed across America to the poet's snowy Northern room as proof of the nation's broad expanse.

title: ORIGINAL POETRY.
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: An editorial headnote praising Coleridge's ode against France's conduct toward Switzerland as the work of a steadfast friend to liberty; prose paratext on freedom and the French Revolution.

title: Orthodoxy
author: Chesterton
summary: Chesterton's major apologetic book recounting how he came to Christian orthodoxy as the answer to a riddle; argues joy is the gigantic secret of Christianity and the modern sceptic is 'born upside down'. Themes: faith and doubt, paradox, wonder, conversion.

title: Osceola
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative elegy of the Seminole chief Osceola's death, who dons his war-dress and paint and silently bids farewell to wife and children before dying.

title: OSORIO
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's tragedy (later 'Remorse'), set in Inquisition-era Granada: the villainous brother Osorio plots his returned brother Albert's death to seize his love and lands; a verse tragedy of fratricide, guilt, remorse, revenge and the Inquisition.

title: OTHELLO
author: Shakespeare
summary: A domestic tragedy in which the Moorish general Othello is poisoned by Iago's deception into murderous jealousy of his innocent wife Desdemona; central themes of jealousy, deception, the outsider, and appearance versus reality.

title: Others May Praise What They Like
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Brief credo praising nothing in art until it has inhaled the atmosphere of the Missouri and western prairie; nationalism, nature, and the artist's American grounding.

title: Otho the Great
author: Keats
summary: A five-act verse tragedy set in the court of Otho I, driven by Conrad's and the femme fatale Auranthe's intrigue, deception, and ambition, ending in betrayal, the prince Ludolph's madness, and death.

title: Our Birthday
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: An essay using birthdays to argue, against Shaw, that human life rests on receptivity, gratitude and inheritance rather than on the modern urge to 'make' a religion or cosmos.

title: Our Mutual Friend
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's last completed novel, organised around the Thames and the Harmon dust-mounds; central themes are money and inheritance, the corrupting power of wealth, false identity and rebirth, social pretension, and redemption through love and self-knowledge.

title: Our Old Feuillage
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A sprawling free-verse catalogue of the American continent, its regions, peoples, animals and labors, celebrating the unity-in-diversity of the democratic nation and the poet's identification with all of it.

title: Out from Behind This Mask (To Confront a Portrait)
author: Whitman
summary: The face as a mask and microcosm condensing the whole universe; the self, identity, the mirror/mask, and the poet greeting the reader across time.

title: Out of May’s Shows Selected
author: Whitman
summary: A catalogue of springtime natural beauty: blossoming orchards, wheat fields, morning freshness, lilac.

title: Out of the Cradle Endlessly Rocking
author: Whitman
summary: The poet's origin-myth: a boy on the Paumanok shore hears a mockingbird mourn its lost mate and the sea whisper 'death'; free-verse elegiac lyric on love, loss, death and the birth of the bard.

title: Out of the Rolling Ocean the Crowd
author: Whitman
summary: A lover figured as a drop from the rolling ocean, met and returned, yet ultimately one with the whole; love, the sea, transience, cosmic unity.

title: Outlines for a Tomb (G. P., Buried 1870)
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Elegy for a philanthropist millionaire (George Peabody) whose gifts conjure visions of provided-for laboring life; death, the tomb, charity, reform, and the common man.

title: OVER MY COTTAGE
author: Coleridge
summary: A cluster of epigrams and fragments on the domestic pleasures of the cottage, love, the moon, a dead beloved, and the nightmare of death-in-life; mixes retreat with melancholy.

title: Over the Carnage Rose Prophetic a Voice
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: A prophetic voice over the carnage declares that comradely affection, not laws or arms, will solve freedom's problems and bind the Union; love, comradeship and democracy.

title: P, Q, R
author: Eliot
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (P–R) listing openings such as 'Polyphiloprogenitive', 'Pipit sate upright' and the Nocturne opening; apparatus to the collected poems.

title: PAIN
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet on bodily suffering contrasting the lost delights of health and nature with the sleepless anguish of disease and tyrannous pain.

title: PANTISOCRACY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Sonnet of utopian hope: leaving past sorrows for a cottaged dell where Virtue strays free; the dream of an ideal community, hope, and visionary nature.

title: PARLIAMENTARY OSCILLATORS
author: Coleridge
summary: A political satire ridiculing wavering, time-serving MPs and Pitt's ministry through the comic simile of ducked fowl; themes of power and corruption and satire of society.

title: Passage to India
author: Whitman
summary: Visionary ode joining the Suez Canal and Pacific railroad to a mystic voyage of the soul back to Asia, primal myth and God; engineering becomes spiritual quest.

title: Patroling Barnegat
author: Whitman
summary: A storm-tossed nocturne of figures patrolling a wild beach watching for a wreck; tightly rhythmic free verse on the sea, storm, night and death.

title: Paumanok
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse apostrophe to Long Island as sea-beauty between ocean and sound; themes of place, the sea and nature.

title: Pen, Pencil and Poison
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Critical biography of Wainewright, the artist-forger-poisoner, exploring the relation of art and crime, the artist and society, and the amorality of beauty.

title: A DEFENCE of PENNY DREADFULS
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: An essay defending cheap popular fiction as the healthy, life-affirming romance of the common man, against the morbid pessimism of educated literature.

title: Pensive on Her Dead Gazing
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse elegy in which the Mother of All bids earth absorb her slain sons and return them in grass centuries hence; themes of war's cost, death, nature and immortality.

title: PERICLES
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late dramatic romance (with George Wilkins) tracing Pericles' wanderings, shipwrecks, the loss and miraculous reunion with his daughter Marina and wife; central to it are the quest/sea-journey, suffering and patience, and providential restoration of the family.

title: PERSPIRATION. A TRAVELLING ECLOGUE
author: Coleridge
summary: Satirical landscape fragment of a dusty hot road and careering 'Aristocracy'; sun, heat, sheep and a glance of class critique.

title: Persuasion
author: Austen
summary: Austen's last completed novel, in which Anne Elliot is reunited with Captain Wentworth years after being persuaded to break their engagement; themes of constancy, second chances, regret, class and the rising navy, with an autumnal, melancholy tone.

title: PHANTOM
author: Coleridge
summary: Dream-vision fragment of a face from which all earthly accident has passed, the pure spirit shining visibly through the body. Themes of soul, idealized beloved and the visionary.

title: PHANTOM OR FACT: A DIALOGUE IN VERSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A dialogue poem on a dream-vision of a lovely form that changes, meditating on dreams, the double, and the passage of years as the dream of life.

title: PHILADELPHIA
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A textual-variants note and alternate versions of the Lessing love-epigram 'Names'/'Die Namen', cataloguing classical pseudonyms and the refrain 'call me thine'.

title: Philosophy for the Schoolroom
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An essay arguing every argument begins with an undemonstrable dogma, listing the unprovable certainties sane men live by; on the foundations of thought, doubt and free will.

title: Philosophy of Furniture
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A satirical aesthetic essay on interior decoration, attacking American 'glare,' glitter and the confusion of cost with beauty, then sketching an ideal tasteful crimson-and-gold chamber.

title: Pickwick
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A critical essay on Dickens's Pickwick as the truest expression of the festive, tolerant 'Merry England' character, against the Puritan caricature of the English.

title: Pioneers! O Pioneers!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A martial chant urging the Western pioneers onward, the open road of conquest and labor, comradeship and death on the march; refrain-driven free verse on American expansion.

title: PITT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A bitter sonnet denouncing Pitt as a Judas-apostate crucifying Freedom; invokes Mercy turned to wrath; themes of political betrayal, corruption, and Christ-imagery.

title: PITY
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet of compassion for a freezing old beggar, offering garment and shelter in imitation of the merciful Christ who befriended the Lazars; themes of pity, poverty, and Christian charity.

title: PLAYS
author: Eliot
summary: Section header for Eliot's verse drama; the present text is Murder in the Cathedral, the martyrdom of Thomas Becket.

title: POEM UPON NOTHING
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty paradoxical compliment to 'Fanny' framed as a poem about nothing, since nothing is softer and more beautiful than she; a jeu d'esprit on paradox and the inexpressible.

title: Poems
author: Chesterton
summary: A collected volume of Chesterton's verse: war poems (Lepanto), love poems, religious/Christmas poems and satirical rhymes; themes of faith, war, patriotism, marriage and joy.

title: The Poet and the Lunatics
author: Chesterton
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A linked cycle of detective/mystery stories featuring the poet Gabriel Gale, who solves crimes through imaginative sympathy; explores sanity, madness, the supernatural and good vs evil.

title: Poets to Come
author: Whitman
summary: Summons future poets to justify him; the speaker hurries back into darkness, expecting the main things from posterity. Prophet-poet, immortality through verse.

title: PONDERE NON NUMERO
author: Coleridge
summary: A gnomic epigram (after Logau) on friendship, that friends should be weighed not counted, and the boaster of many friends never had one.

title: Pongo and the Bull
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A satirical novel of Edwardian high politics and finance, sequel to Mr Clutterbuck's Election, set in a near-future 1925. Prime Minister 'Dolly' and Opposition leader 'Pongo' Pennybunt scheme over an Indian loan while dependent on the financier Duke of Battersea (an antisemitic caricature of a Jewish plutocrat, born plain Mr Barnett). Belloc lampoons the party system, plutocracy and the corruption of public life.

title: Portrait of a Lady
author: Eliot
summary: Dramatic-monologue study of stifled social intimacy, a woman's clinging talk of friendship and the speaker's evasions; alienation, failed feeling, irony and the passage of time.

title: The Praise Of Dust
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric in which despised 'vile dust' speaks back, proclaiming the living glory of the created world and the promise that God will make of dust 'a fairer face than heaven'; on humility, mortality and wonder.

title: A Prayer in Darkness
author: Chesterton
summary: A sonnet of submission in suffering, thanking God that one's wrath cannot harm the world, ending on Christ on the Cross hearing the crickets and being glad; faith, suffering and gratitude.

title: Prayer of Columbus
author: Whitman
summary: Dramatic monologue of a battered, shipwrecked Columbus on a savage shore praying to God in faith, doubt and visionary surrender at the end of life.

title: Preface to 'Kai Lung's Golden Hours'
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: Belloc's introductory essay to Ernest Bramah's Kai Lung's Golden Hours, praising the book as a rare instance of deliberate, achieved construction amid the slipshod, unconstructed writing of the modern age. It argues that construction and economy are the fundamental conditions of excellent and enduring literature.

title: Preludes
author: Eliot
summary: Sequence of urban impressionist lyrics: grimy modern city at dusk and dawn, sordid images, weary souls; spiritual emptiness, squalor and the suffering city.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Austen
summary: Austen's most famous comic novel of manners, in which Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy overcome the pride and prejudice that divide them; themes of marriage, class, first impressions versus reality, and self-knowledge in rural England.

title: PRIESTLEY
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet hailing the exiled scientist-dissenter Priestley as a champion of Religion, Justice, and Nature against superstition and oppression; themes of reform, exile, and rational faith.

title: PROFUSE KINDNESS
author: Coleridge
summary: An epigram on love spread too thin (after Hesiod) and a lament of a hopeless, solitary man mourning a lost beloved wife; loneliness and grief in love.

title: PROGRESS OF VICE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A moralizing poem tracing how vice insinuates itself gradually into the soul, defeats virtue, and drives the wretch by shame and necessity into murder and horror.

title: PROSE VERSIONS OF POEMS, ETC.
author: Coleridge
summary: Prose drafts and glosses behind poems — love likened to the sun, Glycine's song, the self-conscious looking-glass and spider-world figure behind 'Work without Hope', and the dedication to the Ode on the Departing Year; imagination, love and the poet-prophet.

title: Proud Music of the Storm
author: Whitman
summary: Dream-vision in which all the music of nations, religions and nature pours through the sleeper's soul, ending in a charge to write poems bridging Life to Death.

title: PRUFROCK  and Other Observations  1917
author: Eliot
summary: Eliot's first collection (here printing 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock'): modern urban dramatic monologue of paralysis, social timidity, alienation and the failure to act.

title: PSYCHE
author: Coleridge
summary: Epigram on the Greek butterfly-emblem of the soul, contrasting the soul's freedom with the reptile toil of mortal life. Themes of the soul, mortality and Greek myth.

title: The Pun
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: An essay arguing the pun, like rhyme and metaphor, makes completeness of form confirm completeness of idea; a defence of wit and the literary craft against the 'spirit of the age'.

title: QUAE NOCENT DOCENT
author: Coleridge
summary: A penitential lyric lamenting hours wasted in sloth and idle revelry, wishing for time recovered to pursue learning, and concluding that experience and wisdom come only with years.

title: The Club of Queer Trades
author: Chesterton
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A cycle of fantastic detective stories about a club whose members must invent their own trade; mysteries solved by the eccentric ex-judge Basil Grant. Themes: ratiocination, the grotesque, wonder in the everyday.

title: Queries to My Seventieth Year
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse address questioning the coming year as a dim spectre bringing life or death; themes of mortality, old age and time.

title: Quicksand Years
author: Whitman
summary: Short lyric in which amid the dissolving quicksand of politics and shows only the strong-possessed Self/soul remains the final sure substance.

title: THE SONG of QUOODLE
author: Chesterton
summary: A comic song sung by a dog, mocking the 'noselessness of Man' and celebrating the rich animal world of smells closed to human minds; on nature, wonder and the limits of human perception.

title: Race of Veterans
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A brief acclamation of a hardened race of victors and veterans, owning no law but its own; war's forging of a new American people.

title: A Defence of Rash Vows
author: Chesterton
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: An essay defending the great vow (including marriage) as a sane binding of the self against the decadent 'free' man who fears his own mutability; on fidelity, identity and the self.

title: REASON
author: Coleridge
summary: A philosophical-theological fragment defining Reason as the clearing of the mist between God and man, quoting Dante's Paradiso.

title: REASON FOR LOVE’S BLINDNESS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Epigram on why Love is blind: his eyes are in his mind, seeing inward goodness with the heart. Themes of love and inward versus outward worth.

title: RECANTATION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A satirical ballad-fable in which a mob drives an inoffensive ox to madness, allegorizing political panic, mob hysteria and the abuse of the 'mad' label against reformers.

title: RECOLLECTIONS OF LOVE
author: Coleridge
summary: Lyric recalling love amid Quantock hills and the Greta stream, the beloved met as one long loved before. Themes of love, memory, nature and the murmuring river.

title: Reconciliation
author: Whitman
summary: The speaker bends to kiss the white face of his dead enemy, a man divine as himself, as Death and Night wash the world clean; reconciliation, forgiveness and the brotherhood of the dead.

title: Recorders Ages Hence
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Address to future biographers asking to be remembered as 'the tenderest lover' of friends; self-portrait of comradely love, longing and dread of indifference.

title: Red Jacket (From Aloft)
author: Whitman
summary: The ghost of the Native chief Red Jacket looks down on a monument ceremony like one of Ossian's ghosts.

title: REFLECTION ON THE ABOVE
author: Coleridge
summary: A defence of Berengar, who recanted under fear of torture, urging that we judge the man within his dark age and not scorn the timid dawn of truth. Themes: faith and doubt, conscience, martyrdom, progress of truth.

title: REFLECTIONS ON HAVING LEFT A PLACE OF RETIREMENT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A blank-verse conversation poem on leaving the blessed cottage 'Valley of Seclusion' to join the active fight for Freedom and Truth in Christ; themes of retirement vs. duty, nature, faith, and social conscience.

title: RELIGIOUS MUSINGS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A long Miltonic blank-verse meditation written Christmas Eve 1794: the Nativity, divine Love and the 'one Mind', apocalyptic judgement of oppression and the French Revolution, millennial redemption; themes of faith, providence, the One Life, war and its cost, and social injustice.

title: REMORSE
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's Gothic verse tragedy set in Spain during the persecution of the Moors and the Inquisition, in which Ordonio's jealous attempt to murder his brother Alvar is undone when the disguised Alvar returns and stages a sorcerous conjuration to awaken his brother's conscience. It centres on guilt, remorse, revenge, and the supernatural.

title: REPLY TO THE ABOVE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: Verse rejoinder arguing that goodness and greatness are ends, their reward being love, light, calm thoughts, self, God and Death. Moral and consolatory epigram.

title: Return of the Angels
author: Chesterton
summary: An essay arguing the spiritual view of the world, like evolution, is justified as a working hypothesis that makes the whole of reality rational; on faith, the supernatural and method.

title: Reversals
author: Whitman
summary: Brief world-upside-down fragment inverting front and back, bidding the despised offer new propositions; a topos of social reversal.

title: Rhapsody on a Windy Night
author: Eliot
summary: Nocturnal walk through the city governed by street-lamps and the moon; memory dissolved, decayed images, dust and the final 'twist of the knife' of return to routine.

title: RICHARD DUKE OF YORK - (3 HENRY VI)
author: Shakespeare
summary: History play of the full Wars of the Roses: the see-saw struggle between York and Lancaster, the murder of York, the savagery of Margaret, the brief reign of Edward IV, and the emergence of the scheming Richard of Gloucester. Themes of revenge, ambition, kingship, fate, and the horror of civil war.

title: RICHARD II
author: Shakespeare
summary: Lyrical history play, entirely in verse, on the deposition and murder of the introverted King Richard II by Bolingbroke. Central themes: kingship and legitimacy, the divine right and fall of a king, identity, time, and the deposition's political resonance.

title: RICHARD III
author: Shakespeare
summary: History/tragedy charting the deformed Machiavel Richard of Gloucester's murderous rise to the throne and his fall at Bosworth. Central themes: ambition, power and corruption, conscience and guilt, the providential end of the Wars of the Roses.

title: The Song of Right and Wrong
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A comic drinking-song contrasting honest wine with cowardly cocoa and teetotal 'windy waters'; a satirical celebration of conviviality and the moral seriousness of drink.

title: Rise O Days from Your Fathomless Deeps
author: Whitman
summary: The poet, schooled by storms and wilderness, exults as warlike Democracy rises out of the cities; an ecstatic, stormy hymn to the war and democratic energy.

title: Roaming in Thought (After reading Hegel)
author: Whitman
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A two-line free-verse epigram after Hegel: the little Good hastens to immortality while the vast Evil merges and dies; on good vs evil, immortality and the natural order.

title: Robert Browning
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Chesterton's critical biography of Browning, celebrating the poet's optimism, vitality, marriage and the grotesque density of his art; a study of imagination and the artist.

title: Robert Louis Stevenson
author: Chesterton
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Chesterton's critical biography of Stevenson, defending him against detractors and reading his romance and gesture-style as an unconscious Christian witness to innocence, the Fall and joy against modern realism.

title: ROBIN HOOD
author: Keats
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: Ballad-like lyric lamenting that the green merry days of Robin Hood and Marian are gone, displaced by hard money; nostalgia, the lost greenwood and an elegy for old England.

title: Rodney Stone
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: A coming-of-age novel narrated by Rodney Stone, a Sussex boy taken to Regency London by his fashionable uncle Sir Charles Tregellis. Interweaving Rodney's own maturation with the boxing career of his friend Boy Jim, the novel recreates the world of bare-knuckle prize-fighting and Regency society, alongside a Gothic mystery involving a vanished lord and a haunted house.

title: The Rolling English Road
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A comic-elegiac ballad celebrating the crooked English road made by a drunkard, set against Roman straightness; ends contemplating 'the decent inn of death' and Paradise. Themes of Englishness, the open road, mortality and merry resignation.

title: Romance
author: Poe
summary: A short lyric contrasting the gentle paroquet 'Romance' of childhood with the tumultuous 'Condor years' of adulthood, lamenting lost leisure for poetry; on memory, time and the poet's vocation.

title: ROMEO AND JULIET
author: Shakespeare
summary: Lyric tragedy of the star-crossed young lovers of feuding Verona houses, ending in their double suicide and the families' reconciliation. Central themes: romantic love, fate, the feud, the conflict of love and death, youth.

title: Roots and Leaves Themselves Alone
author: Whitman
summary: Calamus poem offering scents, leaves and 'love-buds' that flower only if the reader brings warmth; nature, leaves, flowers and love as organic exchange.

title: Roots of the World
author: Chesterton
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A parable in which a boy tries to uproot an indestructible plant (religion/Christianity), wrecking the whole world but never the plant. An allegory defending faith against secularist and evolutionist attack.

title: Rotarians - (1927)
author: Chesterton
summary: A set of satirical epigrams mocking the Rotary Club's empty business-praise, using the wheel as emblem of circular argument and St Catherine's martyrdom for contrast. Satire of commercialism and modern boosterism.

title: Round the Fire Stories
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: A collection of macabre and mysterious short stories designed for fireside reading, ranging across tales of terror, crime, the uncanny, and unexplained horror, in the vein of Doyle's non-Holmes mystery writing.

title: Round the Red Lamp
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Domestic and Social Fiction · Romantic Love · Class
summary: A collection of medical-life short stories, 'facts and fancies' told from a doctor's-eye view of Victorian practice. Stories range from the gentle comedy of an old-fashioned country doctor and a student's first operation, to grim tales of surgical horror, addiction, and the darker side of medicine, including the macabre 'Lot No. 249' and 'The Case of Lady Sannox.'

title: RUFA
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram (after Lessing) on Rufa and her lap-dog, with a barbed twist on which is the dainty beast.

title: The Runaway Abbot
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: A biographical narrative of the young Thomas Aquinas refusing rank to become a humble Friar, kidnapped by his noble brothers and resisting temptation. Themes of vocation, humility, and the medieval clash of pride and sanctity.

title: S, T, U
author: Eliot
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (S–U) listing openings including 'The winter evening settles down', 'Time present and time past' (Burnt Norton) and Practical Cats lines; apparatus to the corpus.

title: Sail out for Good, Eidolon Yacht!
author: Whitman
summary: Death imagined as the soul's eidolon-yacht sailing out from solid earth onto infinite free waters, framed as entrance to the truest voyage rather than an ending.

title: Salome
author: Wilde
summary: Wilde's one-act biblical tragedy in lyrical prose, dominated by the moon, the femme fatale's lust for the prophet Iokanaan, the dance of the seven veils, and the severed head, fusing desire and death.

title: Salut au Monde!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Vast catalogue-poem saluting all peoples, lands, religions and labors of the globe; cosmic democracy, comradeship of humankind, the sea, nature and the common man.

title: SAMUEL DANIEL
author: Coleridge
summary: Daniel's verse-epistle (adapted by Coleridge for The Friend) on law, justice and the discord in men, invoking King Alfred who joined kingship to goodness and gave law authority; reflection on justice, malice and order.

title: The Outline of Sanity
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Chesterton's central Distributist treatise arguing for widely-distributed private property against both Capitalist monopoly and Socialism, attacking big business, machinery and the distrust of the common man.

title: Savantism
author: Whitman
summary: Sees all results of everyday life nestling and obligated, the poet bringing his songs along like a father to ancestors; nature, time, identity.

title: The Scandal of Father Brown
author: Chesterton
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A collection of Father Brown detective stories in which the humble priest-detective solves crimes through moral and psychological insight rather than mere ratiocination, exposing deception and defending sin's penitents.

title: Scenes From "Politian"
author: Poe
summary: An unfinished blank-verse verse-drama set in Renaissance Rome: the melancholy Earl Politian loves the ruined, vengeance-bound Lalage, swears to slay her betrayer Castiglione, building toward tragedy.

title: Scented Herbage of My Breast
author: Whitman
summary: Calamus meditation where leaves of the breast become tomb-leaves; love and death are inseparable, death the real reality; comradeship, death, melancholy.

title: SCHILLER
author: Coleridge
summary: Schiller's Dithyrambe: the gods never come alone; Bacchus, Amor and Phoebus fill the earthly hall, and the mortal poet begs Hebe for the cup of immortal joy and nectar; classical-mythological lyric of wine, joy and the divine.

title: SCHILLER: DER EPISCHE HEXAMETER
author: Coleridge
summary: Schiller's epigrammatic couplets on metre itself, figuring the epic hexameter as a streaming wave and the distich as a fountain rising in the hexameter and falling in the pentameter; metapoetic verse on poetic form.

title: The Secret of Father Brown
author: Chesterton
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A framed collection of Father Brown stories in which the priest reveals his 'secret' method: solving crime by imaginative empathy with the criminal's soul rather than scientific deduction. Detective fiction with theological depth.

title: The Secret People
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A historical ballad voicing the silent, dispossessed common people of England across centuries of Norman conquest, Reformation plunder, Trafalgar and modern plutocracy, warning 'we have not spoken yet'. Themes of social injustice, patriotism and the common man.

title: SELF-KNOWLEDGE
author: Coleridge
summary: A meditative poem on the Delphic maxim 'know thyself', concluding that man is an unknowable fluxion and should rather strive to know God.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Austen
summary: Austen's 1811 social novel of the Dashwood sisters Elinor and Marianne, contrasting reasoned restraint with romantic feeling through courtship, betrayal and marriage; a satire of manners, money and propriety in genteel English society.

title: SENTIMENTAL
author: Coleridge
summary: A mock-sentimental lyric likening a corn (foot bump) on Angelina's toe to a rose with a thorn, plus a punning epigram on Mr. Baker the buck; parody of sentimental verse using the rose-and-thorn motif.

title: SEPARATION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Love-lyric (after Cotton) of a soldier valuing true inward love over wealth and birth, unable to bear parting from Asra. Themes of love, separation and inward worth versus outward form.

title: The Equality of Sexlessness
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A polemical essay from GK's Weekly attacking modern notions of sex-equality as a flight from motherhood and the family into wage-slavery, satirising progressive 'fraternity' of the sexes. Social criticism defending the home.

title: Shadow-A Parable
author: Poe
summary: A plague-haunted company in ancient Ptolemais confronts a shadow speaking with the voices of the dead; a meditation on death, pestilence and the inescapable presence of the departed.

title: Shakspere-Bacon’s Cipher
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A mystical lyric finding in every old song, object, and life a hidden cipher of meaning infolded behind appearance, the book of nature read for secret import.

title: Sharing Eve’s Apple
author: Keats
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A playful seduction song urging a blushing maiden to seize the prime of youth and share the apple before it is too late; carpe diem, desire, innocence and the Eden allusion.

title: George Bernard Shaw
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Chesterton's critical biography of George Bernard Shaw, examining him as Irishman, Puritan, progressive, critic, dramatist and philosopher; a witty study of ideas, drama and modern thought through a friendly antagonist.

title: Sherlock Holmes: A Drama in Four Acts
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: A stage play co-written with William Gillette, combining elements of several Holmes stories into an original plot. Holmes is drawn into the schemes of the criminal Larrabee gang, who hold captive a young woman, Alice Faulkner, possessing compromising letters, while Holmes's old nemesis Professor Moriarty plots his destruction.

title: Shirley
author: Bronte
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Charlotte Bronte's 1849 social-historical novel set in Yorkshire during the Luddite frame-breaking riots of the Napoleonic-war years; through mill-owner Robert Moore and the heiress Shirley Keeldar and Caroline Helstone it treats industrial unrest, the condition and constraint of women, class conflict and love.

title: The Shop Of Ghosts
author: Chesterton
summary: A fantastical essay in which the narrator meets a dying Father Christmas in a toyshop, visited by the ghosts of Dickens, Steele and Ben Jonson, who declare the spirit of Christmas has always been dying yet never dies. Wonder, tradition and immortality.

title: Shut Not Your Doors
author: Whitman
summary: Demands a place in proud libraries for his war-born book whose drift is everything; the book/writing, the artist and society, war.

title: Silence
author: Poe
summary: A sonnet on the two-fold silence of body and soul, personifying the corporate silence of the grave ('No More') and warning of its nameless, dreadful counterpart.

title: Silence-A Fable
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A Demon recounts how he cursed a desolate Libyan landscape first with tumult then with silence, driving a solitary Roman figure to flight; a parable of desolation, the supernatural and the terror of silence.

title: The Unpardonable Sin
author: Chesterton
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet on love, in which the speaker swears to smite even prophet or angel who fails to revere a woman's love as sacred. Themes of romantic love as religion and reverence.

title: SIR JOHN DAVIES ON THE IMMORTALITY OF THE SOUL
author: Coleridge
summary: Davies's metaphysical stanzas, adapted by Coleridge in Biographia Literaria, on the soul transforming bodies into spirit and abstracting universal forms from particular things.

title: Sir Nigel
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: A prequel to The White Company, set at the start of the Hundred Years' War. Young Squire Nigel Loring, of an impoverished but noble Surrey family feuding with Waverley Abbey, breaks a fierce warhorse, wins his knightly spurs, and sets out to seek chivalric adventure and honor in the service of King Edward III.

title: SIR THOMAS MORE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A collaborative history play (with a Shakespearian scene) dramatizing Thomas More's quelling of the Ill May Day anti-foreigner riots, his rise to Lord Chancellor and his martyrdom for refusing the King's demands; central themes of obedience, conscience and martyrdom.

title: Six British Battles
author: Belloc
summary: A study of six battles in which British arms took part — Blenheim, Crecy, Tourcoing, Waterloo, Malplaquet and Poitiers — each analysed as an incident within its campaign and its governing political object. Belloc insists that military success can be measured only in terms of civil policy, and reconstructs the terrain, manoeuvre and action of each engagement. A work of narrative military history stretching from the Hundred Years' War to Napoleon.

title: The Skeleton
author: Chesterton
summary: A short lyric in which Death laughs among the flowers, revealing death as 'the good King's jest' hidden carefully by God. A joyful, paradoxical meditation on mortality.

title: Skepticism and Spiritualism
author: Chesterton
summary: An essay on the logic of belief, arguing that exposed fraudulent mediums do not disprove the supernatural and distinguishing religious passion from scientific investigation. Faith, doubt and the supernatural.

title: Sketches by Boz
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's early collection of sketches and tales of London everyday life and people; its centre is the comic, satirical and sympathetic observation of the city, its streets, characters, and social types.

title: Skimbleshanks: the Railway Cat
author: Eliot
summary: Galloping comic narrative of the railway cat who patrols and supervises the Night Mail; joyful light verse on order and the journey.

title: SLEEP AND POETRY
author: Keats
summary: Long programmatic poem on sleep, dream and the poet's vocation, defining Keats's ambition to pass from the realm of Flora to the agonies of human hearts; imagination, poetic immortality and the artist's mission.

title: Small the Theme of My Chant
author: Whitman
summary: Declares his theme: the single self and the en-masse, the whole human form, sung for the New World, reaching out to the reader.

title: Antichrist, or the Reunion of Christendom: An Ode
author: Chesterton
summary: A satirical ode mocking F. E. Smith's claim that Welsh Disestablishment shocked Christendom, contrasting his parochial politics with the real suffering of Christians abroad. Satire, faith and politics.

title: SNOW DROP.
author: Coleridge
summary: An earlier draft and textual variants of 'The Snow-Drop', with editorial framing and Mrs. Robinson's original, on the frail flower immortalized by enchantress-song.

title: So Long!
author: Whitman
summary: The valedictory closing poem of Leaves of Grass, announcing future democratic persons and the poet's bodily merging with the reader at death; themes of democracy, immortality of art and mortality.

title: Social Reform B.C
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A polemical essay tracing Birth Control to Malthus's reactionary answer to Godwin, arguing it is a capitalist device to lower wages and oppress the poor, opposed to genuine social reform and the family wage.

title: Some Words with a Mummy
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A galvanized Egyptian mummy, Count Allamistakeo, debates modern Americans and deflates 19th-century faith in progress, democracy and science; a satire blending the grotesque with critique of progress.

title: SOMETHING CHILDISH, BUT VERY NATURAL
author: Coleridge
summary: A tender lyric of separation written in Germany, wishing for a bird's wings to fly to the beloved and finding union only in dreams and sleep.

title: Sometimes with One I Love
author: Whitman
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Brief lyric on the fear of unreturned love resolved by the insight that out of unrequited love come these songs; love, unrequited love and the making of art.

title: Song
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A lyric addressed to a bride on her wedding day, whose blush kindles a fiercer flame of unrequited love and jealous loss in the speaker.

title: Song at Sunset
author: Whitman
summary: An ecstatic free-verse hymn of gratitude praising existence, the body, nature and the splendor of death at life's sunset; themes of wonder, joy and mortality.

title: Song for All Seas, All Ships
author: Whitman
summary: A recitative for the sailors of all nations and a spiritual flag of man elate above death; free-verse on the sea, ships, heroism and comradeship across nations.

title: Song: Hush, hush! tread softly! hush, hush my dear!
author: Keats
summary: A clandestine night-song of lovers tiptoeing past a jealous old guardian to a stolen tryst. It joins secret desire, night, and the rose with the topos of love evading the jealous watcher.

title: Song: I had a dove and the sweet dove died
author: Keats
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A short song mourning a pet dove that died, perhaps of grieving over its tethered captivity. It treats grief, death, and birds, with a hint of love's confinement.

title: Song of Four Faeries - Fire, Air, Earth, and Water -
author: Keats
summary: A dialogue-song among four elemental fairy spirits (fire, air, earth, water) full of nature imagery, courtship and elemental opposition in an enchanted fairy world.

title: Song of Myself
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman's great 52-section epic of the self merging with all humanity and nature; identity, body and soul, democracy, death and rebirth, ecstatic catalogues. Foundational free-verse epic.

title: Song of Prudence
author: Whitman
summary: Doctrine that every deed has consequences beyond death, charity and personal force the only investments; soul, immortality, conscience, and the body-soul bond.

title: Song of the Answerer
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: Portrait of the poet-prophet as universal 'Answerer' welcomed by all nations and trades, who settles justice and immortality; the poet as prophet, the common man, democracy and the artist.

title: Song of the Banner at Daybreak
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: A polyphonic dramatic lyric (Poet, Pennant, Child, Father, Banner) in which the war-flag, valueless yet supreme, demands devotion above peace and wealth; patriotism, war and sacrifice.

title: Song of the Broad-Axe
author: Whitman
summary: The axe as emblem of labor and civilization across history, from the European headsman to the American builder; a free-verse meditation on work, democracy, and the strong common person.

title: Song of the Exposition
author: Whitman
summary: Summoning the Muse from old Europe to modern industrial America, exalting labor, invention, the Union and peace over war; a patriotic free-verse ode to a new democratic culture.

title: Song of the Open Road
author: Whitman
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: Expansive free-verse hymn to the open road as image of freedom, self-reliance and democratic fellowship; the road, the journey, comradeship and the self.

title: Song of the Redwood-Tree
author: Whitman
summary: A dying California redwood chants its death-song, gladly yielding to a coming superber human race; free-verse on nature, mortality, the West, and democratic destiny.

title: Song of the Universal
author: Whitman
summary: A song of the universal good and the seed of perfection in all things, evolution toward the ideal and immortality, with America as the scheme's culmination; free-verse spiritual ode.

title: Song: Spirit here that reignest!
author: Keats
summary: A two-part invocation song addressing first a mournful spirit then a Bacchanal spirit of revelry, written into a volume of Beaumont and Fletcher. It pairs melancholy with festive wine and song.

title: Song: The stranger lighted from his steed
author: Keats
summary: A ballad-like song of a stranger who kisses a lady's hand, lips and maid before riding off, closing with a rapt vow of adoration over a sleeping beloved. Its matter is desire, kissing, and amorous worship.

title: SONG TO BE SUNG BY THE LOVERS OF ALL THE NOBLE LIQUORS COMPRISED UNDER THE NAME OF ALE
author: Coleridge
summary: A drinking song in dialogue praising ale ('Nappy') as nectar, declaring drinkers as blest as the Olympian gods and Olympus an ale-house; carpe diem conviviality with classical allusion.

title: Song: ‘If space and time, as sages say’
author: Eliot
summary: Revised twin of the carpe-diem lyric: 'let us live while yet we may' — withered flowers as emblems of the fleeting flowers of life and love.

title: Song: ‘The moonflower opens to the moth’
author: Eliot
summary: Nocturnal lyric contrasting cool white moon-flowers the beloved holds with a longing for warmer 'scarlet' tropic flowers of passion; white-vs-red imagery of chaste versus ardent love.

title: Song: ‘When we came home across the hill’
author: Eliot
summary: Short lyric in which an unfaded landscape contrasts with the faded roses of the beloved's wreath; understated emblem of decay and lost love amid living nature.

title: Songs of Education
author: Chesterton
summary: A bitterly ironic song in which a child celebrates a mother freed from caring for him to labour in industry, satirising the destruction of family by capitalist 'progress' and state schooling.

title: Songs of Action
author: Conan Doyle
summary: A collection of narrative and ballad-style verse (1898) celebrating martial heroism, sport, and adventure, including poems on English archery, historical battles such as Cremona, storming parties, and hunting and sporting life.

title: Songs of Education125
author: Chesterton
summary: A sequence of satirical songs (History, Geography, Higher Mathematics) parodying patriotic-imperial schooling, mocking Empire, plutocratic finance and the propaganda taught to children.

title: SONGS OF THE PIXIES
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Irregular ode in which Devonshire fairies welcome a Faery Queen, celebrating fancy, nature, twilight and the poet's imagination; pastoral supernatural lyric.

title: Songs of the Road
author: Conan Doyle
summary: A 1911 poetry collection combining narrative ballads, philosophic verse, and miscellaneous lyrics, opening with 'A Hymn of Empire' written for George V's coronation year and including reflective pieces on faith, science, and everyday life alongside sporting and adventure verse.

title: SONNET
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Sonnet translated from Marini in which lover and disdainful lady are doomed to burn in hell, love as fire and torment. Baroque conceit of love as damnation.

title: SONNET
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A sonnet distinguishing instinctive grief for a lover or child from the rarer reasoned grief a youth feels for an aged friend's death; themes of grief, friendship, virtue, and piety.

title: Sonnet:
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet (on a dream of Dante's Paolo and Francesca) in which the poet's spirit, like Hermes lulling Argus, flees to the second circle of hell to float with pale-lipped lovers in the storm. It fuses dream, classical and Dantean myth, and doomed love.

title: Sonnet - The Human Seasons
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet allegorizing the four ages of human life as the four seasons of the mind, ending in a wintry decline that is the price of mortal nature. Its themes are transience, mortality, and the seasons of the soul.

title: Sonnet 1
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Shakespearean sonnet opening the procreation sequence; urges the fair youth to breed so beauty's rose does not die, contrasting increase with self-consuming waste.

title: Sonnet 10
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Accuses the youth of murderous self-hate and pleads he make another self for love; beauty should live in offspring.

title: Sonnet 100
author: Shakespeare
summary: The poet rouses his forgetful muse to sing the beloved and satirize decay, giving fame faster than time's scythe wastes life.

title: Sonnet 101
author: Shakespeare
summary: The truant muse is taught to immortalize truth and beauty in verse, making the beloved outlive a gilded tomb.

title: Sonnet 102
author: Shakespeare
summary: Love strengthened though less shown; like Philomel the speaker holds his tongue lest common song dull its dear delight.

title: Sonnet 103
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The muse's poverty: the beloved's own mirror shows more than verse can; inexpressibility of beauty surpassing the poet's art.

title: Sonnet 104
author: Shakespeare
summary: Three years of seasons pass yet the friend seems unaged; beauty steals away imperceptibly like a dial-hand, hinting at mutability.

title: Sonnet 105
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Love defended against idolatry; the verse confined to constancy sings 'fair, kind, and true', love as quasi-religious devotion.

title: Sonnet 106
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Old chronicles of fair knights and ladies were but prophecies of the beloved; present eyes wonder but lack tongues to praise.

title: Sonnet 107
author: Shakespeare
summary: The mortal moon's eclipse endured; love survives and lives in verse as a monument outlasting tyrants' tombs of brass.

title: Sonnet 108
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Nothing new to write, yet like daily prayers the speaker repeats his love, eternal love that weighs not the dust of age.

title: Sonnet 109
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Denying falsehood despite absence and ranging; like a traveller he returns, calling the beloved his rose and his all.

title: Sonnet 11
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Nature's seal-and-print metaphor; wisdom and increase against age and cold decay, urging the youth to print more copies of himself.

title: Sonnet 110
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Confession of having played the motley and strayed; the wanderings proved the beloved his best of love, to whom he now returns confined.

title: Sonnet 111
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Blaming Fortune for public means that stained his name like the dyer's hand; he drinks bitter potions of penance, cured by the friend's pity.

title: Sonnet 112
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The friend's love fills the brand of vulgar scandal; the speaker, deaf as an adder to others, counts the world besides as dead.

title: Sonnet 113
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: In absence the eye is in the mind; every sight, crow or dove, mountain or sea, is shaped to the beloved's feature, the true mind making the eye untrue.

title: Sonnet 114
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The mind crowned with the beloved drinks flattery as alchemy, turning monsters to cherubins; appearance and love's deceiving eye.

title: Sonnet 115
author: Shakespeare
summary: Earlier verses lied saying he could not love more; reckoning time's tyranny, love is a babe that still doth grow.

title: Sonnet 116
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The marriage of true minds: love as an ever-fixed mark and guiding star, unshaken by tempests and not time's fool even to the edge of doom.

title: Sonnet 117
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The speaker confesses neglect and wandering ('hoisted sail to all the winds') but pleads he strove only to prove the constancy of the beloved's love.

title: Sonnet 118
author: Shakespeare
summary: Medicinal conceit: seeking bitter sauces to whet appetite, the speaker sickened himself with new loves and learned that drugs poison him who sickened of the beloved.

title: Sonnet 119
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Siren tears and a madding fever of errors; the benefit of ill is that ruined love rebuilt grows fairer and stronger than before.

title: Sonnet 12
author: Shakespeare
summary: Clock-and-scythe sonnet cataloguing time's ravages on nature; only breeding can brave time's scythe.

title: Sonnet 120
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Mutual trespass: the friend's past unkindness now consoles the speaker for his own; each trespass ransoms the other in reciprocal guilt and forgiveness.

title: Sonnet 121
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Defiant defense of the self ('I am that I am') against the false judgment and slander of others' eyes; identity, conscience and appearance vs reality.

title: Sonnet 122
author: Shakespeare
summary: The beloved's gift (tables/notebook) given away because memory in the brain holds love beyond all date; memory, writing, and time.

title: Sonnet 123
author: Shakespeare
summary: Defiance of Time and its scythe, vowing constancy ('I will be true') against mutability and the deceiving records of time.

title: Sonnet 124
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Love built far from accident, immune to fortune, time and politic chance; constancy of true love against mutability and fortune's wheel.

title: Sonnet 125
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Rejection of outward show and ruined 'bases for eternity' in favor of mutual, free devotion of a true soul; transience, truth, appearance vs reality.

title: Sonnet 126
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Envoi to the lovely boy: Nature's sickle-hour, her audit and quietus; mortality, time, mutability closing the fair-youth sequence.

title: Sonnet 127
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Opening Dark Lady sonnet: black is beauty's heir, mistress's raven-black eyes against cosmetic false beauty; appearance vs reality, the dark mistress.

title: Sonnet 128
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Watching the mistress play the virginals, envying the keys that kiss her hand; desire, music, the body and jealousy.

title: Sonnet 129
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: 'Th'expense of spirit in a waste of shame': the paradox of lust, savage desire, guilt and self-disgust, heaven that leads to hell.

title: Sonnet 13
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The body as a house that must not fall to decay; husbandry through an heir upholds beauty against winter and death's cold.

title: Sonnet 130

title: Sonnet 19
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 20
author: Shakespeare

author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 22
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 23
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 24
author: Shakespeare

author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 26
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 27
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

title: Sonnet 28
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

title: Sonnet 29
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 3
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

title: Sonnet 30
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 31
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 32
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 33
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

title: Sonnet 34
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 35
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

title: Sonnet 36
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 37
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 38
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 39
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet

author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 40
author: Shakespeare

title: Sonnet 41
author: Shakespeare

author: Shakespeare

author: Shakespeare

author: Keats
