cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet at Burns's grave finding the cold beauty of the scene haunted by sickly imagination and the brevity of the northern summer. It mingles mortality, melancholy, and homage to a dead poet.

title: Sonnet: This pleasant tale is like a little copse
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet written at the end of an old poem, comparing the tale to a little copse and praising white simplicity; reading, poetry, nature and the longing for glory.

title: Sonnet to a Cat
author: Keats
summary: A mock-heroic sonnet addressed to an aged battle-scarred cat recalling its hunts and scrapes; comic mock-elevation of an animal subject.

title: SONNET: TO A FRIEND WHO ASKED, HOW I FELT WHEN THE NURSE FIRST PRESENTED MY INFANT TO ME
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A sonnet to Charles Lamb on first seeing his infant, sad at first then thrilled by mother-and-child love; themes of fatherhood, domestic love, and tenderness.

title: Sonnet to a Lady Seen for a Few Moments at Vauxhall
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet recalling a fleeting glimpse of a lady five years past, whose remembered beauty eclipses every present delight; unrequited love, memory, time and the rose.

title: Sonnet to Ailsa Rock
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet apostrophizing the giant sea-rock Ailsa Craig asleep through 'two dead eternities' of air and deep. It evokes the sublime, geological time, and the sea.

title: Sonnet to Byron
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet praising Byron's sweetly sad melody and the melancholy beauty of his verse; a tribute on poetry, sorrow and the artist.

title: Sonnet to Chatterton
author: Keats
summary: An elegiac sonnet mourning the young poet Chatterton, dead before his prime yet now immortal among the stars; grief, the dead poet and posthumous fame.

title: Sonnet to Fanny
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet of desperate erotic supplication demanding the beloved's whole self, soul and body, lest the poet die or lose his purposes; jealous, all-consuming love.

title: Sonnet to Homer
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet on the blind Homer to whom the gods granted inward sight, finding 'light on the shores of darkness'. It celebrates poetic vision, blindness as insight, and Greek myth and the sea.

title: Sonnet to John Hamilton Reynolds
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet to his friend Reynolds wishing each week were an age so as to crowd long life with joys and annihilate time; friendship, time and the desire to bind eternal joy.

title: Sonnet to Sleep
author: Keats
cluster: Guilt · Conscience · Fate and Free Will
summary: A sonnet praying to Sleep, the 'soft embalmer', to seal the soul and save the speaker from gnawing conscience and the returning day. It treats sleep, night, conscience, and the longing for oblivion.

title: Sonnet to Spenser
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet addressing Spenser, pleading the impossibility of matching his poetic fire and asking for time to ripen; the poetic vocation and inspiration.

title: SONNET: TO THE AUTUMNAL MOON
author: Coleridge
summary: An apostrophe sonnet to the autumn moon whose veiling and emerging light becomes an emblem of changeful Hope struggling against Despair.

title: Sonnet to the Nile
author: Keats
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: A sonnet addressing the Nile, questioning whether it is truly fruitful or a desert deceiver, then affirming its green life; nature, the river, Egypt and imagination versus ignorance.

title: SONNET: TO THE RIVER OTTER
author: Coleridge
summary: Sonnet addressing the native brook of childhood; memory, nostalgia and the wish to be a careless child again. Form: sonnet.

title: Sonnet: When I have fears that I may cease to be
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A Shakespearean sonnet on the fear of dying before fulfilling poetic ambition or knowing love, ending alone on the shore of the wide world; mortality, fame, love and transience.

title: Sonnet: Why did I laugh tonight? No voice will tell
author: Keats
summary: A dark sonnet questioning Heaven, Hell and Heart over a mysterious midnight laugh, concluding that 'Death is Life's high meed'. It treats mortality, melancholy, doubt, and the longing for death.

title: Sonnet Written in Answer to a Sonnet Ending thus:
author: Keats
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A sonnet answering Reynolds in praise of blue over dark eyes, celebrating the blue of sky, sea and flowers; beauty, nature, colour and gallant debate.

title: Sonnet Written in Disgust of Vulgar Superstition
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet attacking gloomy church-going superstition, predicting its death and the rebirth of fresh glories; anticlerical critique, faith and doubt, mutability.

title: Sonnet Written in the Cottage where Burns was Born
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet written in Burns's birthplace, the speaker drunk with whisky and homage, musing on mortality and fame at the dead poet's shrine. Its themes are mortality, fame, and the poet's legacy.

title: Sonnet Written upon the Top of Ben Nevis
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet on Ben Nevis's summit where mist over chasm and sky figures man's blindness to hell, heaven, and himself. It treats the sublime, doubt, and the limits of human knowledge.

title: Sonnet-To Science
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet attacking science as a vulture that preys on the poet's heart, banishing the mythological imagination (Diana, the Naiad, the Hamadryad) and dull realities against poetic vision.

title: Sonnets
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Shakespeare's 154 sonnets. The Fair Youth sequence urges procreation, then immortalizes the beloved's beauty against time and decay through the poet's own eternal verse; the later Dark Lady sonnets turn to desire, jealousy and disillusion. Recurrent notes are love and beauty, the ravages of time, appearance versus reality, and art as a defense against mortality.

title: Sonnets and Verse
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's collected poetry, gathering his sonnets alongside lyrical, didactic and grotesque pieces, drinking songs, ballades and religious verse. Recurrent notes are the Catholic faith, the South Country and Sussex, comradeship over wine, mortality and the open road.

title: SONNETS ATTEMPTED IN THE MANNER OF CONTEMPORARY WRITERS
author: Coleridge
summary: Self-parodying sonnets signed 'Nehemiah Higginbottom' mocking fashionable affected melancholy and over-simple poetic mannerisms; a satire of contemporary verse, in sonnet form.

title: SONNETS ON EMINENT CHARACTERS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Headnote and opening of Coleridge's series of sonnets addressed to eminent contemporaries for the Morning Chronicle; occasional sonnet sequence on public figures.

title: Soon Shall the Winter’s Foil Be Here
author: Whitman
summary: Anticipates spring melting winter's icy ligatures, a thousand forms rising from dead clods as the annual play returns.

title: Sounds of the Winter
author: Whitman
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A wintry pastoral of cheerful rural sounds, the old man among them insisting he has not given out yet but keeps up the lilt from his snowy hairs.

title: Spain, 1873-74
author: Whitman
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A free-verse political ode hailing Freedom rising from feudal European ruins, addressed maternally to Columbia; themes of liberty, revolution and the ruins of the old order.

title: Sparkles from the Wheel
author: Whitman
summary: City vignette of a knife-grinder at his wheel throwing golden sparkles, the poet a floating phantom absorbed in the scene; the city, the common man, the wheel, and perception.

title: SPECIMEN OF AN INDUCTION TO A POEM
author: Keats
summary: Fragmentary prelude announcing a tale of chivalry and invoking Spenser; a young poet's romance of knights, ladies and minstrelsy and an apprenticeship in poetry.

title: Spenserian Stanza
author: Keats
summary: A single Spenserian stanza extending The Faerie Queene, in which 'Typographus' reforms the Giant by books and learning to defeat Artegall and Talus. It plays on the power of the book and learning within Spenserian allegory.

title: Spenserian Stanzas on Charles Armitage Brown
author: Keats
summary: A mock-archaic, gently satirical character-portrait of Keats's friend Charles Brown in Spenserian stanzas; affectionate comedy on temperance, abstemiousness and the bachelor's pilgrim-soul.

title: The Spice of Life
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A wide-ranging collection of literary and religious essays (on Dickens, Shakespeare's Macbeth and Lear, detective stories, fragments, faith and place), the title essay written months before Chesterton's death. Literary criticism and the joy of life.

title: Spirit That Form’d This Scene
author: Whitman
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A free-verse lyric set in Platte Canyon defending the poet's wild, ruleless art by analogy to savage Nature; themes of nature vs civilization and the artist.

title: Spirit Whose Work Is Done (Washington City, 1865)
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Invocation to the departing spirit of war to bequeath its rage and pulses to the poet's chants as the soldiers return home and the conflict closes.

title: Spirits of the Dead
author: Poe
summary: A graveyard lyric in which the solitary soul is surrounded in death by the spirits of the dead, amid night, stars and an oppressive supernatural mystery.

title: Spleen
author: Eliot
summary: A poem of urban Sunday ennui: the dull conspiracy of respectable faces, with Life personified as a bald, fastidious figure waiting on the doorstep of the Absolute — boredom and spiritual stasis.

title: Spontaneous Me
author: Whitman
summary: Catalogue of natural and bodily eroticism, love-juice and procreation matched to the chastity of nature; desire, the body, nature, innocence.

title: SPOTS IN THE SUN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: An epigram exposing a confessor's hypocrisy in frequenting a courtesan, plus one on 'Surface' whose memory selectively forgets others' worth; satire of clerical hypocrisy and self-deception.

title: Second Spring
author: Chesterton
summary: A Christmas lyric on the Nativity, where the homeless Christ in the stable makes all men at home; themes of exile, wonder, faith and the longing for a true home.

title: St. Francis of Assisi
author: Chesterton
summary: Chesterton's biography of St. Francis, reading the saint's life of poverty, humility, love of nature and conversion as a divine paradox; an apologetic and devotional study.

title: Staffa
author: Keats
summary: A visionary poem on Fingal's Cave where the speaker meets the spirit of Lycidas, pontiff-priest of a 'Cathedral of the Sea' built by Oceanus. It fuses the sublime, the supernatural, the sea, and Greek myth in a sea-cave setting.

title: Stanzas
author: Keats
summary: A lyric envying the tree and brook their 'sweet forgetting' of past summer, while humans writhe at remembered joy now lost. It treats memory, transience, grief, and the seasons.

title: Stanzas to Miss Wylie
author: Keats
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A pastoral love lyric inviting Georgiana into a faery-haunted bower of roses and shades to hear a tale of love; romantic love, nature and amorous persuasion.

title: Starting from Paumanok
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Long programmatic chant proclaiming the new American bard of democracy, body and soul, sex, religion and comradeship across the continent; sprawling catalogue free verse.

title: Still Though the One I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Dedicates the one (of contradictions) to Nationality while leaving in him the quenchless fire of revolt; democracy, the rebel, identity.

title: STOLBERG
author: Coleridge
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Stolberg's 'Song of a German Boy': a youth begs his father for a sword, dreams only of war and danger, and longs to die proudly for the fatherland; martial lyric of youthful heroism and patriotism.

title: STOLBERG
author: Coleridge
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: Stolberg's 'To the Sea': the blind bard (Homer) stands by the sea while the giant deeds of a golden age sound around him and the Iliad and Odyssey rise singing from the waves; lyric on the poet-prophet, the sea and epic inspiration.

title: STOLBERG
author: Coleridge
summary: Stolberg poem on the birthplace of William Tell, on whom God bestowed warm blood, falcon's eye and free spirit to free his fatherland from the yoke of bondage; patriotic hymn to a national liberator-hero.

title: STOLBERG: HYMNE AN DIE ERDE.
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Stolberg's hexameter 'Hymn to the Earth': the Earth as mother and nurse of countless children, bride of heaven, whose first blush was the first dawn and whose embrace bred teeming life; a sublime pantheistic nature-hymn.

title: STOLBERG: ON A CATARACT
author: Coleridge
summary: Stolberg's German source-poem to a waterfall as an immortal youth pouring from the rock, clothed by the sun in rays of glory; a sublime nature-hymn on water and grandeur.

title: Concerning a Strange City
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An essay arguing that the finite, the concrete 'place', is what truly suggests infinity; a meditation on words, poetry, religion and the concentration of the spiritual into the real.

title: The Strange Music
author: Chesterton
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A love lyric in which the beloved is an unplayed harp of hidden music; themes of unfulfilled love, hope, mortality and the soul's secret promise.

title: Stronger Lessons
author: Whitman
summary: Asks whether one has learned the stronger lessons from those who reject and oppose rather than admire one.

title: The Fallacy of Success
author: Chesterton
summary: A satirical essay attacking the modern cult of 'Success' as the mysticism of money and avarice; social criticism rooted in the Midas myth.

title: A Ballade of Suicide
author: Chesterton
summary: A comic ballade whose refrain ('I think I will not hang myself to-day') turns the contemplation of death into a celebration of life's small wonders.

title: The Sword of Surprise
author: Chesterton
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A devotional lyric praying to be sundered from body, blood and soul so as to marvel at oneself as a stranger; wonder, self-and-soul, grace.

title: SUSETTE
author: Coleridge
summary: A French dramatic song-scene: Lisette is ferried across the water by Colin/Lubin, courtship leads to marriage, with the refrain 'Et vogue la nacelle qui porte mes amours'; a pastoral love-song of courtship and the river crossing.

title: Sussex
author: Belloc
summary: A topographical and historical portrait of the county of Sussex, tracing how its geography — the South Downs, the Weald, the coastal harbours and marshes — shaped its settlement and history from prehistoric trackways through Roman, Saxon and Norman times. Belloc blends geology, history and affectionate landscape description into a study of local English character.

title: Sweeney Agonistes
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Waste Land (Sterility) · Greek Tragedy
summary: Aristophanic melodrama fragment with Orestes/St John of the Cross epigraphs: cards, a coffin, a murder, the hangman; birth-copulation-death and pursuing guilt.

title: Sweeney Among the Nightingales
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Waste Land (Sterility) · Greek Tragedy
summary: Menacing quatrain poem of the apish Sweeney in a sordid tavern under hostile stars, the nightingales evoking Agamemnon's murder; impending violence, debasement and ironic classical parallel.

title: Sweeney Erect
author: Eliot
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Quatrain poem of the brutish Sweeney shaving while an epileptic woman convulses in a brothel; the grotesque, debased sexuality, the body and a mock-classical frame.

title: The Sword of Wood
author: Chesterton
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A Restoration-set short story in which a weaponless schoolmaster defeats a magnetic sword with a wooden cross-shaped stick; faith, paradox, chivalry, the cross.

title: Tales of Terror and Mystery
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: A collection split into 'Tales of Terror' and 'Tales of Mystery,' including the classic horror story 'The Horror of the Heights' (an aviator's fatal encounter with monstrous life in the upper atmosphere), 'The Leather Funnel' (a dream-vision of historical torture), and detective-flavored mystery stories such as 'The Lost Special' and 'The Man with the Watches.'

title: TALLEYRAND TO LORD GRENVILLE
author: Coleridge
summary: A mock-editorial prose preface (signed 'Gnome') framing the satirical verse epistle, lampooning diplomatic cant, Talleyrand and Napoleonic-era politics with ironic learned notes.

title: TALLEYRAND, MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS AT PARIS, TO LORD GRENVILLE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A satirical verse epistle ventriloquizing Talleyrand to Grenville, mocking political apostasy, diplomatic hypocrisy, press suppression and Napoleonic statecraft in mock-heroic couplets.

title: Tamerlane
author: Poe
summary: A dying conqueror's deathbed confession to a friar, lamenting how ambition and pride for the throne of Samarcand cost him his youthful love; a meditation on ambition, lost love and worldly glory's emptiness.

title: Tears
author: Whitman
summary: A nocturnal shore lyric of grief: a ghostly figure weeping unloosed tears like a storm at night; free-verse on grief, the sea, night and hidden sorrow.

title: Teignmouth
author: Keats
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A doggerel song praising the rural Devon landscape of Teignmouth with its brooks, woods and maidens, preferring it to dark literary London. It is a pastoral retreat poem rich in nature and flowers.

title: The Telegraph Poles
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An essay-dialogue in a pine forest contrasting the living crookedness of nature with the deadening straightness of industrial modernity and 'commercial anarchy'.

title: TELL’S BIRTH-PLACE: IMITATED FROM STOLBERG
author: Coleridge
summary: A patriotic hymn celebrating William Tell's birthplace, joining religious blessing, nature, and the heroic liberation of his land from tyrannical slavery.

title: Tests
author: Whitman
summary: Brief free-verse fragment asserting that the soul's inner judgments, not outer authorities or traditions, are the true tests of all things.

title: Thanks in Old Age
author: Whitman
summary: A thanksgiving in old age for life, memories, family, readers and brave men, given as a returning soldier's grateful thanks.

title: That Music Always Round Me
author: Whitman
summary: The speaker awakens to the unceasing cosmic chorus of voices and instruments, hearing in it exquisite meanings and beginning to know the performers.

title: That Shadow My Likeness
author: Whitman
summary: Poet doubts whether the worldly shadow-self is really him, but never doubts his identity among lovers and songs; identity, self and soul, the double.

title: The Ad-dressing of Cats
author: Eliot
summary: Concluding comic verse on how to address a cat with proper respect; light verse with a wry note that cats are much like people.

title: The Adventure of the Tall Man
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: An unfinished Holmes fragment, later completed by other writers, in which a young man is wrongly convicted of murdering his sweetheart's uncle. Holmes exposes a rival suitor's frame-up involving stilts disguised as ladder-marks, then extracts a confession by staging a terrifying apparition of the murdered man.

title: The Adventures of Gerard
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Adventure Fiction · Empire and Imperialism · Peril and Survival
summary: A second series of comic tales narrated by the boastful, gallant Hussar Etienne Gerard, recounting his exploits during the Napoleonic Wars across Europe. Gerard's vanity and self-regard are undercut by genuine bravery, as Doyle satirises both French self-image and English stereotypes of it.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: The first collection of twelve Holmes short stories (1892), including 'A Scandal in Bohemia,' 'The Speckled Band,' and 'The Red-Headed League.' Holmes and Watson solve mysteries of blackmail, theft, and murder through observation and deduction, establishing the classic detective-and-companion formula.

title: THE ALTERNATIVE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A lover's epigram wishing Enna would either truly love him or stop pretending, plus a drinking pun contrasting Spanish wine and Rhine 'gripes'; unrequited love and wine.

title: The Angel of the Odd
author: Poe
summary: A drunken skeptic is plagued by a grotesque liquor-cask spirit who orchestrates a cascade of absurd accidents to punish his disbelief in the improbable; a comic extravaganza on chance and the grotesque.

title: The Angry Street
author: Chesterton
summary: A fantastic parable in which an overworked London street rears up to heaven for justice; satire of mechanical modern life, the supernatural breaking into the city.

title: The Artilleryman’s Vision
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A veteran at home is seized by a midnight vision of battle, hearing the missiles and feeling the old mad joy; war-trauma, memory and the haunting persistence of combat.

title: The Assignation
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A Byronic stranger in Venice and the married Marchesa Aphrodite share a forbidden love that ends in their simultaneous death by poison at the appointed hour; a tale of love-as-religion, doomed passion and aestheticism.

title: The Bad Child's Book of Beasts
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's celebrated 1896 book of cautionary comic verse for children, presenting a bestiary of animals (Yak, Lion, Tiger, Whale, Elephant and more) in short mock-moral rhymes. The tone is nonsensical and gently subversive, parodying the improving children's book while delighting in absurdity.

title: The Ballad of Reading Gaol
author: Wilde
summary: A ballad recounting the execution of a condemned guardsman, meditating on guilt, mercy, the cruelty of prison and Man's justice, and the redemptive figure of Christ, framed by the refrain that each man kills the thing he loves.

title: THE BALLAD OF THE DARK LADIÉ
author: Coleridge
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A medievalising ballad fragment of a forsaken lady awaiting her knight Lord Falkland, who would lead her away by stealth in the dark rather than wed her openly; themes of unrequited love, the fallen woman and deception.

title: The Ballad of the White Horse
author: Chesterton
summary: Chesterton's epic ballad of King Alfred's last stand against the pagan Danes at Ethandune, framed by a vision of the Virgin; the struggle of Christianity and heathenism, heroism, hope without guarantee.

title: The Balloon-Hoax
author: Poe
summary: A fabricated newspaper account of the first transatlantic balloon crossing, presented as fact; a hoax celebrating science, technology and the credulity of the age.

title: The Base of All Metaphysics
author: Whitman
summary: Professor's farewell declaring that beneath Greek and Germanic philosophy and Christ lies 'the dear love of man for his comrade'; comradeship as the ground of metaphysics.

title: The Battle of Life
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's Christmas Book, a love story set on an old battlefield in rural England; central themes are self-sacrificing love, the metaphor of life as a daily battle, sisterly devotion, and the contrast of war's bloodshed with nature's recovery.

title: The Bells
author: Poe
summary: An onomatopoeic lyric tracing the bells of life from merry sledge-bells through wedding-bells to alarm-bells and finally the funereal iron tolling of death; a sonic meditation on time, mutability and mortality.

title: The Birthday of the Infanta
author: Wilde
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: At the Spanish court a deformed dwarf, loved by no one, dances for the Infanta until a mirror reveals his ugliness and his heart breaks; a tragic tale of cruelty, beauty versus ugliness, and the grotesque.

title: The Black Cat
author: Poe
summary: A condemned narrator confesses how alcohol and the spirit of perverseness led him to mutilate and hang his cat and murder his wife, his guilt betrayed by a second cat; a tale of guilt, madness and the grotesque.

title: THE BLOSSOMING OF THE SOLITARY DATE-TREE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A Lament prefaced by a Rabbinical fable of Adam, Eve and Satan; the solitary date-tree symbolizes love denied and the ache of solitariness. Themes of loneliness, unrequited love and the Fall.

title: The Book of the Bayeux Tapestry
author: Belloc
summary: A historical study of the Bayeux Tapestry read as the one surviving pictorial record of the Norman Conquest and the making of medieval Christendom. Belloc argues from costume, heraldry and Wace's Roman de Rou for a twelfth-century date, then narrates the embroidery panel by panel as a symbolic chronicle of Harold, Edward and William.

title: The Boston Evening Transcript
author: Eliot
summary: Brief satiric lyric on the dull, conformist readers of a New England newspaper; satire of bourgeois society, weariness and the deadness of routine.

title: The Bravoes of Market-Drayton
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A true-crime essay collection examining real Victorian murder trials: the 1828 Market-Drayton case of a rustic gang hired to strangle a witness, and the unresolved 1860 murder of the reclusive landlady Mary Emsley. Doyle weighs the trial evidence and questions the reliability of circumstantial proof and capital verdicts.

title: THE BRIDGE STREET COMMITTEE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A mock-syllogistic satire ('Jack Snipe eats tripe') ridiculing the Constitutional Association that prosecuted publisher Richard Carlile for blasphemy; political satire and defence of free expression.

title: The British Campaign in France and Flanders (Volumes I-VI)
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: Doyle's six-volume contemporary history of the British Army on the Western Front, from Mons and the Marne in 1914 through the Somme, Third Ypres, Cambrai, and the victorious advance of 1918, compiled from letters, diaries, and firsthand interviews with soldiers and officers.

title: THE BRITISH STRIPLING’S WAR-SONG IMITATED FROM STOLBERG
author: Coleridge
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A martial war-song in which a youth, fired by ancestral deeds, longs for a sabre to fight and die for his native land as his forefathers did.

title: The Business Man
author: Poe
summary: A self-styled methodical 'man of business' satirizes commercial society by pursuing a series of petty, swindling 'methodical' trades; a satire of money-grubbing and bourgeois respectability.

title: The Calming Thought of All
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Amid changing theologies and philosophies, the earth's silent vital laws continue, a calming natural order.

title: The Canterville Ghost
author: Wilde
summary: A comic-gothic story parodying the haunted-house tale: a centuries-old English ghost is defeated by an unflappable, materialist American family, yet finds release through a child's pity and prayer, ending in genuine grace, forgiveness and the recurrent bloodstain motif.

title: The Cap and Bells
author: Keats
summary: An unfinished comic-satiric faery tale in Spenserian stanzas about Emperor Elfinan's enforced fairy marriage and love of mortal women; mock-epic court satire set in an enchanted Eastern fairyland.

title: The Captain of the Pole-Star, and Other Tales
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: An early collection of supernatural and macabre tales, headed by the title story of a whaling captain haunted (or driven mad) by a ghostly visitant on the Arctic ice, and including 'J. Habakuk Jephson's Statement,' Doyle's fictional solution to the Mary Celeste mystery, and 'The Great Keinplatz Experiment' on mesmeric soul-transfer.

title: The Case of Mr. George Edalji
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: Conan Doyle's investigative pamphlet defends George Edalji, a half-Indian solicitor wrongly convicted of maiming livestock near Great Wyrley, arguing the prosecution was driven by racial prejudice and shoddy police work. Doyle's advocacy helped establish England's Court of Criminal Appeal.

title: The Case of Mr. Oscar Slater
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: Doyle's investigative pamphlet dissects the wrongful murder conviction of Oscar Slater, a German-Jewish immigrant scapegoated for the 1908 bludgeoning of wealthy Glasgow spinster Marion Gilchrist, exposing shaky eyewitness identification and a fatal prosecutorial misstatement.

title: The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: The final Holmes collection (1927), gathering twelve later stories including 'The Mazarin Stone,' 'The Problem of Thor Bridge,' 'The Creeping Man,' and 'The Sussex Vampire.' Holmes, older but undiminished, unmasks jewel thieves, blackmailers, and seemingly supernatural crimes through rational detection.

title: The Cask of Amontillado
author: Poe
summary: A first-person tale of premeditated revenge in which Montresor lures the wine-loving Fortunato into the catacombs during carnival and walls him up alive; its central matter is revenge, deception, and dramatic irony.

title: The Castle Builder - Fragments of a Dialogue
author: Keats
summary: A dialogue fragment of fanciful self-indulgence, the Castle Builder furnishing an imaginary luxurious moonlit room crowded with art, skulls and roses; imagination, art, mortality and the grotesque.

title: The Centenarian’s Story
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative poem in which a Revolutionary War centenarian recalls Washington's defeat at Brooklyn and the slaughter of the young brigade; war, sacrifice, memory and national continuity.

title: The Chimes
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's Christmas 'Goblin Story' in which a poor ticket-porter, Trotty Veck, is shown by the spirits of the bells visions of despair and degradation among the poor; central themes are social injustice, poverty, the dignity of the common man, and redemption from despair into hope.

title: The City Dead-House
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Meditation on the unclaimed corpse of a dead prostitute as a ruined yet immortal 'house,' tenement of a soul; death, the body, compassion, and the outcast.

title: The City in the Sea
author: Poe
summary: A visionary lyric depicting a doomed city of the dead where Death reigns enthroned among ruined towers before the whole town sinks into the sea; its themes are mortality, ruin, and apocalyptic decay.

title: THE COCKTAIL PARTY
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Waste Land (Sterility) · Greek Tragedy
summary: Eliot's drawing-room comedy with a spiritual core, loosely modelled on Euripides' Alcestis: a psychiatrist-guardian (Reilly) directs the Chamberlaynes toward reconciliation in ordinary marriage and Celia toward a vocation of sanctity and martyrdom.

title: The Coliseum
author: Poe
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A meditative blank-verse poem on the ruins of the Roman Coliseum that turns the fallen monument into a lesson on the passing of glory and the enduring power of memory; an ubi sunt / sic transit reflection.

title: The Colloquy of Monos and Una
author: Poe
summary: A dialogue between two reunited souls after death describing the sensations of dying and bodily decay, framed by a critique of mechanical progress and modern civilization.

title: THE COMEDY OF ERRORS
author: Shakespeare
summary: Farcical Plautine comedy of two sets of identical twins separated at sea, producing a cascade of mistaken identity in Ephesus before family reunion. Central themes: identity, appearance vs reality, marriage, the comic recovery of lost kin.

title: The Coming of the Fairies
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Doyle assembles correspondence and expert testimony defending the authenticity of the Cottingley fairy photographs taken by two Yorkshire girls, arguing they offer photographic proof of a hidden spirit world and situating the case within Theosophist and Spiritualist belief.

title: The Commonplace
author: Whitman
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Whitman sings the cheap, common, democratic wisdom of everyday life and the open air, with an appended dark catalogue probing the place of evil in earth's scheme.

title: THE COMPLAINT OF NINATHÓMA:FROM THE SAME
author: Coleridge
summary: Ossianic lyric of a lamenting maiden in a sea-cave visited by the ghost of the departed; lyric on grief, loss and the consoling/disturbed dream of the dead.

title: THE COMPLIMENT QUALIFIED
author: Coleridge
summary: A backhanded satirical epigram to Eliza on marrying a fool, plus appended epigrams defining the epigram itself and mocking liars, misers and a devilish lord.

title: THE CONFIDENTIAL CLERK
author: Eliot
summary: Eliot's drawing-room comedy after Euripides' Ion, turning on mistaken parentage and disputed identity: Sir Claude, Lady Elizabeth and the clerk Colby discover who is whose lost child, while Colby seeks a true vocation over an inherited one.

title: The Conqueror Worm
author: Poe
summary: A theatrum-mundi lyric in which human life is staged as a tragedy watched by weeping angels, its hero the devouring Worm; a despairing allegory of mortality, sin, and madness.

title: The Conversation of Eiros and Charmion
author: Poe
summary: A dialogue of disembodied souls recounting the destruction of the Earth by a comet that burned away the atmosphere; an apocalyptic tale of cosmic annihilation and the afterlife.

title: The Cricket on the Hearth
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's third Christmas Book (1845), a domestic fairy-tale novella in which the chirping hearth-cricket acts as a household guardian spirit; centres on the carrier John Peerybingle, his young wife Dot, a mysterious lodger, and a near-mistaken jealousy resolved into marital fidelity, charity, and festive reconciliation.

title: The Crime of the Congo
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A polemical expose of the atrocities committed under King Leopold II's Congo Free State, cataloguing forced labour, mutilation, and mass killing of Congolese people for rubber profits, and calling on the international community to intervene.

title: The Critic as Artist
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Critical dialogue arguing that criticism is itself a creative art; a sustained aesthetic meditation on beauty, imagination, contemplation and the artist and society.

title: The Crown Diamond
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: A one-act Sherlock Holmes play in which Holmes lures the ruthless Colonel Sebastian Moran and his accomplice into his Baker Street rooms using a wax dummy decoy, forcing a confession over the theft of the great yellow Crown Diamond.

title: The Cruise of the Nona
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's reflective travel-memoir framed as a solo sail of his boat the Nona along the coasts of Britain. Storms and near-drownings alternate with meditations on fear and courage, faith, small kingdoms versus great states, words, politics and the past, so the voyage becomes a model of one human life.

title: The Cultivation of Christmas Trees
author: Eliot
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Meditation on the child's wonder at Christmas as religious feast; gratitude, awareness of death, the first and second coming, fire/light imagery.

title: The Dalliance of the Eagles
author: Whitman
summary: On a river walk the poet witnesses two eagles mating in mid-air, a fierce gyrating wheel then parting; a free-verse lyric on birds, nature, desire and motion.

title: The day is gone, and all its sweets are gone!
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet on the vanishing of a day of love at nightfall, cataloguing fading sensual delights; transience of beauty and erotic pleasure with a devotional 'love's missal' close.

title: THE DAY-DREAM FROM AN EMIGRANT TO HIS ABSENT WIFE
author: Coleridge
summary: Dream-vision in which an exiled husband almost sees his absent wife before a child's laugh wakes him to weeping. Themes of love, separation, dream and longing.

title: The Dead Emperor
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: America bends in mourning for a dead Emperor, condoling less the crown than a good old man and patriot.

title: The Dead Tenor
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Elegy for an operatic tenor whose singing voice taught the poet, his memory dropped like an autumn leaf into the grave.

title: The Dealings of Captain Sharkey and Other Tales of Pirates
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Adventure Fiction · Empire and Imperialism · Peril and Survival
summary: A collection of swashbuckling sea tales centered on the sadistic pirate Captain Sharkey, who repeatedly outwits captains, governors, and avengers sent against him through disguise and cold cunning, alongside further stand-alone stories of blue-water adventure and mystery.

title: The Death of Saint Narcissus
author: Eliot
summary: Visionary free-verse poem of a self-absorbed ascetic who, transformed through tree, fish and girl, becomes a dancer before God and dies pierced by burning arrows; self-love, martyrdom, mortification of the flesh, and the gray rock of The Waste Land.

title: THE DEATH OF THE STARLING
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Imitation of Catullus mourning a pet bird; the Loves and Venus weep for the dead starling. Mock-elegy on death of a beloved bird.

title: THE DEATH OF WALLENSTEIN
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's blank-verse translation of Schiller's historical tragedy in five acts, dramatizing the imperial general Wallenstein's treason against the Emperor, his betrayal by trusted officers, and his assassination. Its central matter is ambition, fate (Wallenstein's trust in his star), political power and corruption, and the cost of war.

title: The Debatable Case of Mrs. Emsley
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: An essay reexamining the 1860 unsolved murder of the reclusive London landlady Mary Emsley, weighing the circumstantial evidence that hanged plasterer George Mullins and questioning whether justice was truly served.

title: The Decay of Lying
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Aesthetic critical dialogue arguing art over nature, lying as art, and that life imitates art; a manifesto of art for art's sake rich in paradox and epigram.

title: The Defendant
author: Chesterton
summary: A collection of paradoxical 'defence' essays (penny dreadfuls, detective stories, skeletons, baby-worship, patriotism) defending despised or common things; wonder, paradox, social satire.

title: THE DELINQUENT TRAVELLERS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A satirical verse on the post-war fashion for restless travel and tourism, mock-celebrating transported convicts as the truest 'delinquent travellers'. Themes: satire of society, the journey, social criticism.

title: THE DESTINY OF NATIONS: A VISION
author: Coleridge
summary: A long visionary blank-verse poem on Freedom, the symbolic Book of Nature, polar legends, and Joan of Arc's prophetic vision of war, peace, and revolution; themes of providence, freedom, war and its cost, imagination, and the warrior-maid.

title: The Devil in the Belfry
author: Poe
summary: A comic satire in which a devilish stranger invades an orderly clockwork Dutch borough and overturns its obsession with time and routine; a burlesque of bourgeois order turned upside down.

title: THE DEVIL’S THOUGHTS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A satirical ballad in which the Devil strolls the earth admiring human vice (pride, greed, hypocrisy, the slave-trade, prisons), a grotesque social satire of England's corruption.

title: The Devon Maid
author: Keats
summary: A flirtatious pastoral song wooing a Devon dairy maid amid meads, hills and flocks toward a kiss on the heather. It blends rural nature, desire, and amorous play.

title: The Devoted Friend
author: Wilde
summary: A satirical fable in which a rich Miller exploits and finally causes the death of little Hans while endlessly preaching the virtues of 'true friendship', mocking hypocrisy and false friendship.

title: The Disintegration Machine
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Science Fiction · Discovery · Reason vs the Supernatural
summary: Professor Challenger and journalist Malone investigate a Latvian inventor's claim to have built a machine that can disintegrate and reassemble matter, a weapon he intends to sell to a hostile foreign power, until Challenger turns the invention on its treacherous creator.

title: The Dismantled Ship
author: Whitman
summary: An old battered dismasted ship, after all its voyages, lies rusting and mouldering in a nameless bay, an image of aged decline.

title: The Doings of Raffles Haw
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Science Fiction · Discovery · Reason vs the Supernatural
summary: A mysterious, fabulously wealthy stranger, Raffles Haw, builds a palatial house near the village of Tamfield and befriends the impoverished artist Robert McIntyre and his sister Laura. Haw's fortune, secretly derived from a chemical process for transmuting base metal into gold, brings ruin as much as good, corrupting those around him and exposing the moral hazards of unearned wealth.

title: The Domain of Arnheim
author: Poe
summary: A reflective tale-essay on landscape gardening as the highest art, in which a wealthy aesthete builds an earthly paradise; its matter is beauty, the sublime, and the artist's creation of an ideal garden.

title: The Dry Salvages 1941
author: Eliot
summary: Third Quartet: the river as brown god and the sea of many voices, time and the Annunciation, prayer to the Virgin; the sea, water, time, faith, conversion.

title: The Duc de L'omelette
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A flippant comic tale in which a dandified Duc dies of gourmandise, finds himself before the Devil in Hell, and wins his soul back at cards; a satire of foppery and a playful treatment of damnation.

title: The Duchess of Padua
author: Wilde
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Wilde's second play, a five-act blank-verse revenge tragedy set in Renaissance Padua; Guido is driven to avenge his murdered father against the tyrannical Duke, falls into transgressive love with the Duchess Beatrice, and the pair die together amid guilt, sin and redemption. Central themes: revenge, forbidden love, guilt and mercy, the corrupt tyrant.

title: THE DUNGEON
author: Coleridge
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A dramatic blank-verse fragment denouncing the cruelty of imprisonment and invoking healing Nature instead of punishment; themes of social injustice, reform and nature's redemptive power.

title: The Dying Veteran
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A Revolutionary War veteran on his deathbed cries to return to his old battle-life, rejecting the present age of peace.

title: The Edge of the Unknown
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Doyle's final book is a passionate defense of Spiritualism, opening with a detailed portrait of his troubled friendship and rivalry with Houdini, whom Doyle believed to be a suppressed physical medium turned medium-baiter. It goes on to recount ghost sightings, psychic mail, and personal encounters offered as evidence for survival after death.

title: THE ELDER STATESMAN
author: Eliot
cluster: Guilt · Conscience · Fate and Free Will
summary: Eliot's last verse drama: the retired public man Lord Claverton is confronted at a rest-home by ghosts of his guilty past (Gomez, Mrs. Carghill) and, through confession and his daughter's love, finds contrition, self-knowledge and peace before death.

title: The Emerald of Catherine the Great
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A comic anti-detective novel (dedicated to Maurice Baring) tracing a great emerald, gift of Catherine the Great to an English sea-captain, down through the rising fortunes of the de Bohun family to its loss at a Hertfordshire country house. Belloc promised a detective story 'with nothing to find out', using the mystery frame to satirize social climbing, political careers, and the mania for talismans and pedigrees.

title: THE EOLIAN HARP
author: Coleridge
summary: A major conversation poem at Clevedon: the wind-harp prompts the pantheistic 'one Life' vision of nature as organic harps swept by an 'intellectual breeze', checked by pious humility; themes of imagination, the One Life, faith, love, and nature.

title: The Eve of Saint Mark
author: Keats
summary: A narrative fragment of the maiden Bertha poring over an illuminated legend of St Mark in a quiet cathedral town at dusk, her giant shadow looming. It evokes medieval piety, the book, martyrdom, and an eerie hush in a medieval English setting.

title: THE EVE OF ST. AGNES
author: Keats
summary: Spenserian-stanza medieval romance: on a bitter winter's eve Porphyro steals into the castle of his enemies to win Madeline during her St Agnes dream-vision, and the lovers flee into the storm; romantic love, dream, and a cold gothic-medieval setting.

title: THE EXCHANGE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Slight love-lyric on lovers exchanging hearts and the speaker trembling before the maiden's father. Romantic love in song form.

title: The Exploits of Brigadier Gerard
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Adventure Fiction · Empire and Imperialism · Peril and Survival
summary: A series of comic adventure tales narrated by the aging Hussar Etienne Gerard, who fought through Napoleon's campaigns and remains gloriously convinced of his own bravery, swordsmanship, and irresistibility to women. Through his boastful, self-deluding first-person voice Doyle gently satirizes both French vanity and English notions of the French, while delivering genuine derring-do — duels, sieges, and narrow escapes across Napoleonic Europe.

title: The Facts in the Case of M. Valdemar
author: Poe
summary: A pseudo-scientific horror tale in which a dying man is mesmerized at the point of death and held suspended for months until his sudden, grotesque dissolution; themes of death, the uncanny, and bodily decay.

title: THE FADED FLOWER
author: Coleridge
summary: Sonnet on a plucked withered flower as melancholy emblem of a ruined woman (Abra) destroyed by selfish love; flowers, decay, the fallen woman, transience.

title: The Fall of Hyperion
author: Keats
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: An unfinished blank-verse dream-vision in which the poet, guided by the priestess Moneta, beholds fallen Saturn's titanic ruin and is interrogated on the difference between poet and dreamer; meditation on poetry, suffering and the fall of the gods.

title: THE FALL OF ROBESPIERRE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A historic closet drama by Coleridge and Southey on the fall of Robespierre, dramatizing tyranny, conspiracy, the rhetoric of Liberty, ambition and the bloody self-consuming course of the French Revolution.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
author: Poe
summary: A gothic tale of the doomed twins Roderick and Madeline Usher, premature burial, hereditary madness and the literal collapse of their decaying house; a study in terror, the double, and the uncanny.

title: THE FAMILY REUNION
author: Eliot
summary: Eliot's verse drama transposing the Oresteia onto an English country house: Harry, Lord Monchensey, haunted by the Eumenides and by guilt over his wife's death, seeks expiation and spiritual deliverance while his family clings to surfaces.

title: The Field Bazaar
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: A short comic Holmes vignette, written for an Edinburgh University charity magazine, in which Holmes deduces from Watson's demeanor and a single letter that Watson has been asked to contribute to a university bazaar in aid of the cricket field. The piece is a playful, self-aware parody of the familiar Baker Street breakfast-table deduction scene, followed in this volume by the companion miniature tale 'How Watson Learnt the Trick.'

title: The Firm of Girdlestone
author: Conan Doyle
summary: John Girdlestone and his brutal son Ezra run a lucrative African trading firm and treat every act, including charity, as a calculated investment. Their cynical pursuit of a dying friend's fortune for his orphaned daughter sets in motion a chain of financial schemes, deception, and eventually an unforeseen murder.

title: The First Dandelion
author: Whitman
summary: A spring nature lyric celebrating the season's first dandelion as innocent and renewing after winter.

title: THE FIRST PART OF THE CONTENTION - (2 HENRY VI)
author: Shakespeare
summary: History play dramatizing the disintegration of weak King Henry VI's realm: the fall of Duke Humphrey, the rise of York's claim, Queen Margaret's intrigues, and Jack Cade's bloody populist rebellion. Themes of kingship and legitimacy, ambition, order vs chaos, and civil war.

title: The Fisherman and his Soul
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy tale in which a young fisherman cuts away his shadow-soul to wed a mermaid; the disembodied, heartless Soul becomes his tempting double, dramatizing desire versus soul, body versus spirit, and the sea as the realm of pagan love against the Priest's Christian condemnation.

title: The Flying Inn
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: A comic satirical novel in which a fashionable English elite imposes a quasi-Islamic prohibition, and an innkeeper and an Irish soldier roam England with a keg and an inn-sign defending old liberties, ale and the common man; satire, anti-progressivism, English patriotism.

title: The Forest Reverie
author: Poe
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A lyric likening the felling of a primeval wood to the wasting of love, from whose grief spring 'the rare and radiant flowers of song'; nature imagery turned to loss redeemed by poetry.

title: THE FOSTER-MOTHER’S TALE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A dramatic blank-verse fragment from Osorio narrating a foundling who becomes a learned heretic, is imprisoned, escapes and vanishes among savage men in the New World; themes of nature vs civilization and freedom.

title: The Four Men
author: Belloc
summary: Subtitled 'A Farrago', a mixed prose-and-verse account of a four-day walk across Sussex by four companions - Myself, Grizzlebeard, the Sailor and the Poet - who are really facets of Belloc himself. An elegiac celebration of the beloved home county, friendship and wine, shadowed by the knowledge that all beloved things must pass.

title: The Free Press
author: Belloc
summary: A Distributist tract analysing how the great capitalist newspaper press, dependent on advertising subsidy, corrupts news and opinion and lets a few unaccountable proprietors usurp real political power. Belloc contrasts this with the small independent 'Free Press' (The New Age, the New Witness) whose power lies in telling the truth.

title: The French Revolution
author: Belloc
summary: An interpretive history that expounds the Revolution not as chronicle but as thesis — its sovereign-community political theory, its leading characters, its phases, its military aspect, and above all its quarrel with the Catholic Church. Belloc, an avowed Catholic sympathetic to Republican theory, argues the religious conflict is the key to understanding the whole event. Character studies of the King, Queen, Mirabeau, Danton, Marat and Robespierre anchor the analysis.

title: The Future of Canadian Literature
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A 1914 lecture delivered to the Canadian Club in Montreal, in which Doyle reflects on the historical rhythms of literary flowering, arguing that great literature only follows a long 'seed-time' of national struggle and practical achievement. He offers advice on style, vocabulary, patience with criticism, and predicts that Canada's coming literary greatness will follow, not precede, its material and nation-building labors.

title: The Gadfly
author: Keats
summary: A comic squib invoking the gadfly's sting to torment lawyers, politicians, and pious scolds, mocking public figures. It is a verse satire of society through the figure of the fool and animal imagery.

title: THE GARDEN OF BOCCACCIO
author: Coleridge
summary: A reverie roused from melancholy vacancy by a gift-engraving of Boccaccio's garden, conjuring a locus amoenus of Florence, Ovid, myth and Poesy/Philosophy. Themes: imagination, the garden/pastoral retreat, memory, melancholy, art.

title: THE GENTLE LOOK
author: Coleridge
summary: Sonnet of lost love and vanished hope, the beloved's smile recalled in dream amid melancholy and a vale of tears; lyric on memory and transience.

title: The Girondin
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A historical novel opening in Bordeaux in August 1792, following young Georges Boutroux, nephew of a prosperous wine merchant, as private family quarrels give way to the tumult of the Revolution. Belloc sets an ironic, well-bred domestic comedy against the gathering violence of the Republic.

title: The Glass Walking Stick
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A posthumous selection of Chesterton's Illustrated London News essays on history, architecture, art, monarchy and national tradition. Central matter: the romance and meaning of history, defence of tradition against fashionable progress, and the imaginative recovery of the past.

title: The Gold-Bug
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A tale of ratiocination in which Legrand decodes a pirate's cryptogram to unearth Captain Kidd's buried treasure; a detective-style story driven by cipher-breaking, gold, and analytic reasoning.

title: THE GOOD, GREAT MAN
author: Coleridge
summary: Epigrammatic complaint that the good and great man rarely gains honour or wealth he merits. Theme of worldly injustice versus inner worth.

title: The Great Boer War
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: Doyle's detailed contemporary history of the Second Boer War (1899-1902), tracing the origins of the Boer nations from Dutch and Huguenot settlers through the Great Trek and the annexation disputes that led to conflict with the British Empire. The book narrates the war's major battles and sieges chapter by chapter, going through sixteen revised editions as the campaign unfolded.

title: The Great Inquiry
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A political satire (reported 'by H. B.' and illustrated 'by G. K. C.') burlesquing Joseph Chamberlain's 1903 Tariff Reform commission as a mock official inquiry. A parade of self-interested manufacturers, farmers and ministers give absurd evidence, exposing protectionism and imperial preference as a racket dressed in patriotic language.

title: The Great Keinplatz Experiment and Other Tales of Twilight and the Unseen
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Domestic and Social Fiction · Romantic Love · Class
summary: A collection of early Doyle short stories exploring the supernatural and the uncanny, opening with 'The Brown Hand,' in which a dead Indian patient's ghost returns nightly seeking his amputated hand, and 'The Usher of Lea House School,' a tale of blackmail and menace beneath a schoolmaster's genteel surface. The other tales range across mesmerism, doubles, and unexplained hauntings at the borderland of the visible world.

title: The Great Shadow
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: Scottish border farmer Jock Calder of West Inch narrates his youth during the Napoleonic Wars, his rivalry with his strong friend Jim Horscroft for the love of his flirtatious cousin Edie, and his eventual service against Napoleon's invasion threat, culminating at Waterloo. The novel blends border-country domestic life with the looming national fear of Bonaparte, 'the great shadow' over Europe.

title: The Green Flag and Other Stories
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Adventure Fiction · Empire and Imperialism · Peril and Survival
summary: A collection opening with the title story of a disaffected Irish regiment redeemed by loyalty to its own green flag during a desert battle against dervishes, followed by pirate tales of the sadistic Captain Sharkey, a boxing story ('The Croxley Master'), and other adventure and romance pieces ranging from the Napoleonic era to colonial Africa.

title: The Green Overcoat
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A comic farce novel in which the timid Professor Higginson, tempted by the Devil, steals a magnificent green overcoat on a rainy night and is promptly swept into a bungled kidnapping. The stolen garment drives an escalating chain of Edwardian mischance and deception across a provincial manufacturing town.

title: The Guards Came Through and Other Poems
author: Conan Doyle
summary: A First World War poetry collection whose title piece celebrates British soldiers holding the line at Hill 70 until the Guards break through, followed by patriotic and elegiac verses on England's endurance, Haig's advance, the trenches at Ypres, and the dead of the war.

title: The Gully of Bluemansdyke and Other Stories
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Adventure Fiction · Empire and Imperialism · Peril and Survival
summary: Doyle's early colonial adventure tales, led by the title story in which vigilante troopers and miners hunt down murderous bushrangers on the Australian goldfields, alongside stories of a reforming Bible-quoting camp preacher, a murderer's confession, and other frontier and mystery pieces.

title: The Happiest Day
author: Poe
cluster: Vanitas · Contemptus Mundi · Vanity of Worldly Things
summary: Early lyric of disillusionment in which the speaker renounces past hopes of pride and power, dwelling on the transience of youth and the soul-destroying alloy hidden in joy.

title: THE HAPPY HUSBAND
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lyric fragment on married love, the very name of Wife a pledge of more than passing life. Themes of marriage, fidelity and joy.

title: The Happy Prince
author: Wilde
summary: Fairy-tale allegory of charity and self-sacrifice: a gilded statue and a swallow give away gold and jewels to the city's poor and are redeemed as the two most precious things by God.

title: The Haunted House
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A satirical novel following Rackham, an old Sussex squire's house, as the amiable, improvident Henry Maple slides into debt and his methodical solicitor brother William, prodded by an ambitious wife, quietly engineers its transfer through mortgages and interest. Belloc anatomizes the decline of the landed gentleman and the cold arithmetic of modern finance devouring inherited land.

title: The Haunted Man and the Ghost's Bargain
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's last Christmas Book (1848), a supernatural moral allegory in which the chemist Redlaw accepts a phantom double's bargain to forget all sorrow, wrong and trouble, only to spread coldness and lose his humanity until love and memory restore him; themes of memory, grief, redemption and the prayer 'Lord keep my Memory green.'

title: The Haunted Palace
author: Poe
summary: Allegorical poem in which a once-radiant palace (the mind of monarch Thought) falls to evil and madness, dramatizing decay, mutability and the fall from a golden past.

title: The Hedge and the Horse
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A satirical novel built on the proverb that one man may steal a horse while another may not look over a hedge — a fable of Fate's injustice in money and reputation. It opens with the tale of the reclusive New York usurer John Scott Guthrie, who amasses a fortune and settles a watched, teetotal-conditioned allowance on his feckless English nephew Wilfred Straddle.

title: The Hippopotamus
author: Eliot
summary: Satiric quatrain fable contrasting the lowly fleshly hippopotamus with the smug, worldly True Church; satire of the institutional church, the flesh-spirit divide and ironic apotheosis.

title: The Historic Thames
author: Belloc
summary: A historical-topographical study (1907) of the River Thames, arguing that England was built upon the framework of her rivers and that the Thames, as highway, boundary and site of the first crossing at London Bridge, shaped the nation's economic, military and political life. Belloc reads geography — fords, marshes, gravel spurs, parish boundaries — as the substrate of English history.

title: THE HISTORY OF KING LEAR - THE QUARTO TEXT
author: Shakespeare
summary: The Quarto text of Shakespeare's great tragedy: an aged king divides his kingdom by flattery, is cast out into the storm by ungrateful daughters, and descends into madness; themes of kingship, filial ingratitude, madness, nature, and order versus chaos.

title: The History of Spiritualism, Volume I
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Doyle's history of the Spiritualist movement from its precursors, beginning with the visionary scientist-mystic Swedenborg and the Hydesville rappings of the Fox sisters, through early American and English mediumship, D. D. Home, and the scientific investigations of Sir William Crookes, arguing for the movement's genuineness as a new revelation.

title: The History of Spiritualism, Volume II
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: The concluding volume surveys later mediums led by Eusapia Palladino, the Society for Psychical Research, ectoplasm and spirit photography, Continental Spiritualism, and the movement's wartime and religious significance, ending with Doyle's account of the Spiritualist vision of the afterlife.

title: THE HOLLOW MEN 1925
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Waste Land (Sterility) · Greek Tragedy
summary: Litany of straw-stuffed paralysed men in a dead cactus land where 'the Shadow' falls between idea and act; spiritual emptiness, paralysis, despair, fading prayer and the famous whimpering end of the world.

title: The Holocaust of Manor Place
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A true-crime account of William Godfrey Youngman, who in 1860 murdered his mother, two young brothers, and his sweetheart Mary Streeter in a lodging house, apparently for a small insurance payout, followed by a transcript of his Old Bailey trial and execution; Doyle frames it as a case study in pathological selfishness.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: Sherlock Holmes and Watson investigate the death of Sir Charles Baskerville, apparently from fright, amid an old family legend of a diabolical hound haunting the moor. As the new heir Sir Henry arrives at Baskerville Hall, Holmes uncovers a very human plot hiding behind the supernatural terror.

title: THE HOUR WHEN WE SHALL MEET AGAIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A love-lyric composed in illness and absence longing for reunion with the beloved, with the rose-and-dawn emblem of mistress healing flower; themes of romantic love and longing.

title: THE HOUR-GLASS
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's free version of Amaltei's Latin epigram (via Jonson): the sands of the hour-glass were once a swain who loved in vain, so lovers' ashes find no rest; epigram on time, death and unrequited love.

title: The Imp of the Perverse
author: Poe
summary: Essay-tale on the self-destructive impulse to act against one's own interest; a murderer's compulsion to confess illustrates guilt, conscience and perverse human nature.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest
author: Wilde
summary: Farcical comedy of manners turning on Bunburying/double identities, courtship and marriage, and a sustained satire of late-Victorian London society.

title: THE IMPROVISATORE OR, JOHN ANDERSON, MY JO, JOHN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A dialogue and verse meditation on enduring married love that survives age, with the lost 'boon' figured as a withered evergreen, ending in Contentment after Hope's death. Themes: enduring love, marriage and fidelity, ageing, hope and disappointment.

title: The Island of the Fay
author: Poe
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Meditative prose-poem on solitude and natural scenery in which a solitary dreamer watches a fairy circle an island, her vanishing shadow allegorizing the cycle of life and death.

title: The Jews
author: Belloc
cluster: Familiar Essay · Paradox · The Common Man
summary: A polemical essay on 'the Jewish problem', in which Belloc argues that the Jews form a permanently alien nation within Europe and that the only stable remedy is open mutual 'recognition' and segregation rather than absorption or persecution. Though it repudiates massacre and expulsion, the book rests on and propagates antisemitic premises about Jewish separateness, finance and Bolshevism.

title: The Journey
author: Conan Doyle
summary: An allegorical verse-drama in which personified guides — Faith (in its many sectarian forms), Reason, Science and Inspiration — squabble over the true path to the City Beautiful, while a Man and Woman climb the mountain of life accompanied by Sorrow and the memory of their dead child. It dramatizes Doyle's own tension between organized religion, rationalism, and the consolations of an afterlife.

title: The Judgment of England
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A short epigrammatic poem reversing Goldsmith's line on wealth and decaying men, indicting industrial commerce: now 'Men accumulate and Wealth decay'. Themes of social injustice, the decay of the common man, and a prophetic note of judgment.

title: THE KEEPSAKE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A blank-verse lyric in which faded summer flowers contrast with the embroidered keepsake (rose and forget-me-not in Emmeline's hair), a token pledging fidelity and remembrance until spring.

title: THE KISS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Love lyric pleading for a kiss, with the Zephyr and rose as erotic emblem and the maid's whispered 'No' that endears consent; desire, the rose, the western gale.

title: THE KNIGHT’S TOMB
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A short ubi sunt lyric asking where Sir Arthur O'Kellyn's grave lies; his bones are dust and his sword rust. Themes: mortality, transience, the grave.

title: The Lake -- To--
author: Poe
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Lyric of youthful solitude at a wild lake whose nocturnal terror becomes a tremulous delight, mingling death, imagination and a private Eden of the lone soul.

title: The Land of Mist
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Professor Challenger's daughter Enid and journalist Edward Malone investigate London's Spiritualist churches and mediums, initially as sceptical reporters. Challenger himself, still grieving his wife, is gradually confronted with evidence that shakes his rigid materialism, as Doyle uses the novel to argue for the truth of Spiritualism.

title: The Landscape Garden
author: Poe
summary: Aesthetic tale-essay in which the immensely wealthy poet Ellison devotes his fortune to landscape-gardening as the supreme art, theorizing beauty, nature and the artist's creation of an intermediate Nature between man and God.

title: The Last Galley
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: A volume of historical 'impressions and tales' ranging from the destruction of Carthage's last fleet by Rome, to Nero's rigged singing contest at Olympia, to a Christian slave's martyrdom under Domitian, plus eight independent short stories. Doyle uses vivid historical vignettes to dramatize the rise and fall of empires as a warning parable for Britain.

title: The Last Invocation
author: Whitman
summary: Gentle prayer for the soul at death to be wafted noiselessly from the fortressed house of the body, unlocking the doors of mortal flesh and love.

title: The Last of the Legions and Other Tales of Long Ago
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: A companion historical collection opening with the title story, in which the Roman viceroy of Britain must withdraw every legion, dooming his British petitioners to the chaos of invasion; it then regathers 'The Last Galley' and other Doyle historical tales under a new arrangement. The stories together meditate on empires that rise, overreach, and inevitably fall.

title: The Literary Life of Thingum Bob, Esq
author: Poe
summary: Comic mock-autobiography satirizing the corruption, puffery and vanity of the American literary marketplace through the rise of a fatuous, self-glorifying editor.

title: The Lost Tools of Learning
author: Sayers
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: In this 1947 Oxford lecture Sayers contends that modern schooling teaches a multitude of "subjects" but fails to teach children how to think, leaving them defenceless against propaganda, advertising and sloppy argument. Her remedy is to revive the medieval Trivium—Grammar, Dialectic and Rhetoric—as the true tools of learning, matching each to a natural stage of the child's development (the Poll-parrot, the Pert and the Poetic ages). The sole end of education, she insists, is to teach people how to learn for themselves, so that any subject becomes an open door.

title: The Lost World
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Science Fiction · Discovery · Reason vs the Supernatural
summary: Young journalist Edward Malone, seeking heroic deeds to win the woman he loves, joins the irascible Professor Challenger's expedition to a South American plateau where dinosaurs and ape-men still survive. The party must fight both prehistoric monsters and hostile natives to prove Challenger's incredible claims true.

title: The Love Affair of George Vincent Parker
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A nonfiction case-study essay on a real Victorian murder: a sensitive, unworldly young man, jilted by his fiancee Mary Groves under family pressure, stabs her to death during a final meeting and calmly confesses, provoking a legal debate over his sanity. Doyle uses the letters and trial record to examine the psychology of the 'passionate criminal' driven by disappointed love rather than greed.

title: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock
author: Eliot
summary: Dramatic monologue of a timid, ageing modern man unable to ask his 'overwhelming question'; themes of alienation, paralysis, time, mortality and self-consciousness in an urban evening.

title: THE MAD MONK
author: Coleridge
summary: A ballad set by Etna in which a mad monk's song laments lost steady loveliness and confesses the murder of his beloved Rosa, a Gothic study of grief, guilt and madness.

title: THE MADMAN AND THE LETHARGIST
author: Coleridge
summary: A Greek epigram (Anthologia Graeca) on a madman and a lethargist as figures of folly, with an appended Guarini madrigal-dialogue of Faith, Hope and Charity calling souls back to God; epigram and devotional allegory.

title: THE MADMAN AND THE LETHARGIST
author: Coleridge
summary: Satirical verse-fable of a madman (Jacobin France) and a lethargist (John Bull) curing each other by chance, with a political-satiric edge. Themes of madness, satire and folly.

title: The Man from Archangel and Other Tales of Adventure
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: A miscellany opening with adventure tales — including a young officer outwitted and then forgiven by his own disguised general in the Sudan, and a recluse's uneasy encounter with a mysterious woman on the Yorkshire moors — followed by a separate suite of medical-life stories drawn from Doyle's own experience as a doctor. Together the tales range from imperial derring-do and Gothic unease to the everyday drama of the surgery.

title: The Man of the Crowd
author: Poe
summary: A convalescent narrator obsessively follows an enigmatic old man through nocturnal London, finding in his refusal to be alone the unreadable type and genius of deep crime amid the modern crowd.

title: The Man That Was Used Up
author: Poe
summary: Grotesque satire in which a celebrated war-hero general proves to be a literal assemblage of manufactured prosthetics, mocking the age's faith in mechanical progress and hollow public reputation.

title: The Man Who Knew Too Much
author: Chesterton
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A cycle of detective stories whose disillusioned sleuth Horne Fisher 'knows too much' about the corruption of the governing class to expose the crimes he solves. Themes: political corruption, the cost of knowledge, justice frustrated, and patriotic self-sacrifice.

title: The Man Who Made Gold
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A comic satirical novel in which a drug-addled Oxford undergraduate dabbling in occult alchemy appears to succeed in making gold, throwing the world of banking and finance into panic. Belloc lampoons modern science, academic pomposity, and the greed of high finance through the collision of medieval magic and the modern atom.

title: The Maracot Deep
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Science Fiction · Discovery · Reason vs the Supernatural
summary: Professor Maracot, assistant Cyrus Headley, and mechanic Bill Scanlan descend in a steel diving-chamber to the bottom of the Atlantic to survey an oceanic trench. Their hawser is severed by a monstrous crustacean and they sink to the sea floor, where they discover the still-inhabited ruins of Atlantis and are rescued by its people, who possess strange sciences and face a resurgent evil sorcerer.

title: The Masque of the Red Death
author: Poe
summary: Allegory in which Prince Prospero's sealed revel cannot escape the plague: the masked Red Death enters the seven chambers as the ebony clock tolls, asserting Death's illimitable dominion.

title: The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: Eleven Sherlock Holmes stories from 1893-94, including the vanishing racehorse of 'Silver Blaze' and, in 'The Final Problem,' Holmes's fatal confrontation with his arch-enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls. The collection was intended by Doyle to end the Holmes series permanently.

title: THE MERCHANT OF VENICE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A tragicomedy in which the merchant Antonio borrows from the Jewish moneylender Shylock on a bond of a pound of flesh; it turns on the conflict of justice and mercy, the casket-test courtship of Portia, and the trial scene resolved by Portia disguised as a lawyer.

title: The Mercy of Allah
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A satirical frame-narrative in the manner of the Arabian Nights, in which the immensely rich merchant Mahmoud recounts to his nephews the swindles, thefts and lucky frauds by which he rose from a kicked-out boy to a 'Captain of Industry.' Each tale ironically credits his crimes to the Mercy of God. Belloc uses the Oriental disguise to lampoon modern capitalist acquisition and the sanctification of greed.

title: THE MERRY WIVES OF WINDSOR
author: Shakespeare
summary: A middle-class citizen comedy set in Windsor in which Falstaff's attempts to seduce two married women are turned against him by the wives' ingenious tricks; a farce of disguise, jealousy, and bourgeois domestic life.

title: The Mind of the Maker
