author: Sayers
summary: Writing not as an apologist but as a professional writer, Sayers argues that the Christian creeds' statements about God the Creator are, when tested against direct experience, an exact description of the human creative mind. Every act of making is a threefold, Trinitarian structure—the Creative Idea (the Father), the Creative Energy or Activity incarnate in matter (the Word), and the Creative Power responding in the reader's soul (the Spirit)—three distinct "Persons" that are yet one work. From this analogy she illuminates free will, miracle, the problem of evil, self-expression, and the worth of work, and she diagnoses a modern age that mistakes life for a "problem" to be solved rather than a creation to be made.

title: The Missing Masterpiece
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A comic satirical novel in which an English squire's crippled son, a preternaturally exact copyist, becomes entangled with a bohemian Paris artist and a forged 'masterpiece', driving a farce of art, publicity and money. The narrative carries antisemitic caricature in its depiction of landlords and financiers.

title: The Model Millionaire
author: Wilde
summary: Short story in which a beggar-model is secretly a millionaire who rewards a poor lover's charity, satirising money, appearance versus reality and the artist's world.

title: The Modern Manichee
author: Chesterton
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A dense lyric portraying the modern man who denies sin and so turns the whole green world merciless and obscene; an attack on a pessimistic, life-hating heresy. Themes: sin and the fall, the denial of guilt, and a corrupted vision of nature.

title: The Modern Traveller
author: Belloc
summary: A comic narrative poem in which a boastful adventurer, interviewed by the press, recounts a disastrous African expedition financed as a company flotation and staffed by scoundrels Commander Sin and Captain Blood. Belloc satirises imperial exploration, jingoist journalism and the speculative money behind colonial 'ventures.'

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: The foundational tale of ratiocination in which C. Auguste Dupin solves a baffling Parisian double murder through analytical deduction, inaugurating modern detective fiction.

title: The Mystery
author: Chesterton
summary: A short lyric of cosmic wonder: the speaker marvels at sun, sky and the lost first heaven, ending 'I wonder at not wondering'. Themes: wonder and gratitude, the fall from Eden, and the inexpressibility of praise.

title: The Mystery of Cloomber
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: John Fothergill West's family settles near a Wigtownshire manor let to General Heatherstone, an Anglo-Indian officer barricaded in dread of a supernatural vengeance stemming from a Buddhist mystic's curse laid on him during the Afghan campaigns decades earlier. The mystery builds toward the arrival of three Eastern avengers who claim the debt owed for a long-ago betrayal.

title: The Mystery of Edwin Drood
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's unfinished detective/mystery novel set in the cathedral town of Cloisterham: John Jasper, an opium-addicted choirmaster, is secretly obsessed with Rosa Bud and implicated in the disappearance of his nephew Edwin Drood, framing a double-life study of guilt, the divided self, and respectable hypocrisy amid imagery of decay, crypts, opium dens, and the gritty city.

title: The Mystery of Marie Roget
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A Dupin ratiocinative tale reconstructing the murder of a young Parisian shop-girl (mirroring the real Mary Rogers case) through probability, newspaper analysis, and armchair detection.

title: The Mystic Trumpeter
author: Whitman
summary: An unseen ghostly trumpeter conjures in turn the feudal past, love, war, despair, and finally a redeemed future of universal joy; music as visionary power.

title: The Naming of Cats
author: Eliot
summary: Light comic verse on the three names of cats, the third ineffable name being beyond human discovery; playful on identity and the inexpressible.

title: The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition)
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: A first-person sea-voyage adventure novel of stowaway, mutiny, shipwreck, starvation, cannibalism and a southward quest ending in an apocalyptic Antarctic vision of a white shrouded figure and a silent cataract.

title: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: Poe's only completed novel: a frame-tale sea adventure of stowaway, mutiny, shipwreck, starvation, cannibalism and a hallucinatory voyage to a mysterious all-white Antarctic region. Central themes are terror, the quest into the unknown, and the dissolution of identity at the white limit of the world.

title: THE NETHERLANDS
author: Coleridge
summary: A brief descriptive fragment of the watery Dutch landscape — windmills, willows, fog-transfixing spires and wide water; pure topographical imagism.

title: The New Revelation
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Doyle's 1918 apologetic account of his conversion from medical materialism to conviction in Spiritualism, tracing decades of table-sittings, mediumship, and psychical research literature. He argues that verified communications with the dead confirm survival of the soul and call for a reformed, evidence-based Christianity.

title: THE NIGHT-SCENE
author: Coleridge
summary: A dramatic fragment in blank verse: Earl Henry recounts to Sandoval a passionate night-vow in a moonlit garden bower. Themes: romantic love, vow and fidelity, the sublime of passion.

title: The Nightingale and the Rose
author: Wilde
summary: A nightingale gives her heart's blood to make a red rose for love, only for the gift to be scorned; a fairy tale on self-sacrifice, the worth of love versus utility, and white turning to red.

title: THE NOSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A burlesque mock-ode that hyperbolically apostrophizes a glowing red nose with images of Promethean fire, comets, and hellfire, parodying the lofty sublime ode.

title: The Old Curiosity Shop
author: Dickens
summary: Dickens's sentimental social novel: orphan Little Nell and her gambling-ruined grandfather flee London and the grotesque dwarf Quilp, wandering through England until Nell's celebrated death among graveyard ruins.

title: The Old Gumbie Cat
author: Eliot
summary: Comic narrative of Jennyanydots, the orderly tabby who drills mice and cockroaches by night; joyful light verse on a domestic cat.

title: THE OLD MAN OF THE ALPS
author: Coleridge
summary: A pathetic narrative poem in which an aged Alpine father recounts how his daughter, maddened by her soldier-lover's death in war, dies in a storm; themes of grief and loss, war's cost and consolation through faith.

title: The Old Road: from Canterbury to Winchester
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's 1904 topographical and historical reconstruction of the Pilgrims' Way, the ancient east-west track along the North Downs between Winchester and Canterbury. Part meditation on the primal power of the Road and antiquity, part field diary, he walks and maps the route yard by yard to recover the lived experience of the earliest travellers.

title: THE OUTCAST
author: Coleridge
summary: Sonnet of compassion for a fallen woman cast out to want and scorn by a pitiless world; social injustice, the fallen woman, the outcast, mercy of the great Comforter.

title: The Ox-Tamer
author: Whitman
summary: Pastoral portrait of an illiterate farmer who tames wild oxen by love; celebrates the common man, animals and rural life over books.

title: THE PAINS OF SLEEP
author: Coleridge
cluster: Guilt · Conscience · Fate and Free Will
summary: Confessional lyric of nightmare-ridden sleep, guilt, remorse and self-loathing relieved only by the wish to be loved. Themes of nightmare, conscience and inner hell.

title: The Pallid Wreath
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: An elegiac lyric on memory and grief: a withered funeral wreath kept hanging because the dead friend remains vivid and unfaded in remembrance.

title: THE PANG MORE SHARP THAN ALL: AN ALLEGORY
author: Coleridge
summary: An allegory of lost Hope figured as a vanished faery boy, leaving the playmates Esteem and Kindness, the sharpest pang being Kindness counterfeiting absent Love. Themes: grief and loss, hope, love, the imagination.

title: The Parasite
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: Physiologist Austin Gilroy, a confirmed materialist, is drawn into a mesmeric relationship with Miss Penclosa, a crippled psychic who first proves her powers on his fiancée Agatha and then enslaves his own will, forcing him toward betrayal and violence against everyone he loves. Written as Gilroy's diary, the story tracks his terrified loss of self-control until Penclosa's illness momentarily frees him.

title: The Path to Rome
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's account of his vow-driven walking pilgrimage on foot from Toul in Lorraine across the Alps to Rome, digressing freely on wine, faith, landscape, history and the European soul. Part travelogue, part familiar essay, it is a joyous personal confession of Catholic conviction and love of the common life of Europe.

title: The Persecution of Religion
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An ILN essay arguing that science now persecutes religion, mocking Shaw's 'Back to Methuselah' and Darwinian evolution for abandoning any fixed human ideal. Themes: faith versus a deifying scientism, critique of progress and the Superman, and the need for a permanent standard.

title: THE PICCOLOMINI
author: Coleridge
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Coleridge's blank-verse translation of Schiller's Wallenstein I, set in the Thirty Years' War: the general Wallenstein's growing rebellion against his Emperor, with intrigue, ambition, loyalty and fate; a historical verse tragedy.

title: The Pickwick Papers
author: Dickens
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: Dickens's episodic comic picaresque following Mr Pickwick and his club across England through coaching inns, the Bardell breach-of-promise suit, and the Fleet debtors' prison; a mock-heroic satire of law and society animated by benevolence, good humour and the wit of Sam Weller.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Wilde
summary: Gothic novel of aestheticism in which a Faustian wish keeps Dorian beautiful while a hidden portrait bears the corruption of his soul, exploring beauty, sin, the double, and conscience.

title: THE PICTURE OR THE LOVER’S RESOLUTION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Blank-verse meditation in which the lover flees love through a wild wood, watches a reflected vision break and reform in a pool, and resolves to follow the maid. Themes of love-longing, imagination, illusion and nature.

title: The Poet - A Fragment
author: Keats
summary: A fragment defining the true poet as one equal to king or beggar and able to understand the speech of birds and beasts; the poet, imagination and negative capability.

title: THE POETASTER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A dramatic fragment from Jonson's Poetaster, adapted by Coleridge: a consoling speech on how grief over a love ravished by death cracks the strongest virtue and makes the heart-strings jar.

title: The Poison Belt
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Science Fiction · Discovery · Reason vs the Supernatural
summary: Professor Challenger summons his old comrades from The Lost World to his Sussex home, convinced that Earth is passing through a poisonous belt of ether that will exterminate humanity. Sealed in an oxygen-filled room, the party watches what they believe to be the annihilation of civilization, only to wake into an eerily stilled but ultimately recovering world.

title: The Polish Ideal
author: Chesterton
summary: An essay celebrating Catholic Poland and the civilized cavalier — soldier and poet at once — whose chivalric, providential faith defeated Bolshevist materialism. Themes: heroism and chivalry, faith against mechanistic determinism, and national-religious romance.

title: The Portrait of Mr. W. H.
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A story-essay defending the Willie Hughes theory of Shakespeare's Sonnets, in which a forged portrait, aesthetic faith, and male friendship lead two men to die for a literary idea.

title: The Postmaster General
author: Belloc
cluster: Satirical Novel · Politics and Finance · Edwardian England
summary: A near-future political satire set in a 1960 of Socialist and Anarchist parties, skewering the corrupt marriage of government and finance. Postmaster-General Wilfrid Halterton nervously signs a rigged television-monopoly contract for the financier James McAuley, trading a public charter for his own promised place in the City.

title: The Prairie States
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Compact paean to the prairie states as a new modern garden of creation, a teeming democratic paradise justifying the past.

title: The Prairie-Grass Dividing
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Demand for free, sunlit, audacious companionship modeled on the open prairie-grass; nature, grass, the common man, comradeship and democratic self-reliance.

title: The Professor
author: Bronte
summary: Charlotte Bronte's first novel (written before Jane Eyre, published 1857), the first-person account of William Crimsworth who works his way from trade through teaching in Brussels, falling in love with his pupil-teacher Frances; a sober realist Bildungsroman on self-reliance, work earned by merit, love and self-discipline.

title: THE RAPE OF LUCRECE
author: Shakespeare
summary: Tragic narrative poem in rhyme royal: Tarquin's rape of the chaste Roman matron Lucrece, her grief and suicide, and the political revolution it triggers. Central themes: lust, honour and chastity, guilt, justice and the fall of tyranny.

title: THE RASH CONJURER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: Grotesque comic ballad of a conjurer who raises devils, Lucifer's dam and Antichrist and is dragged toward hell. Themes of the supernatural, the grotesque and damnation in burlesque form.

title: THE RAVEN
author: Coleridge
summary: A ballad-fable told as a Christmas tale in which a raven, his family destroyed by a woodman, exults in revenge when the ship built from his oak is wrecked; themes of revenge, death and nature.

title: The Raven
author: Poe
summary: Poe's signature narrative poem: a bereaved lover, mourning the lost Lenore at midnight, is visited by a talking raven whose 'Nevermore' deepens his grief into despair. Themes of mortality, grief, memory and irrational dread.

title: The Refugees
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: Set at the court of Louis XIV, this historical novel follows Huguenot guardsman Amory de Catinat and his cousin Adele as royal favor turns against Protestants with the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes, driving the Catinat family into exile. Aided by the American frontiersman Amos Green, the refugees flee across the Atlantic into the wilderness of New France.

title: The Remarkable Rocket
author: Wilde
summary: A satirical fairy tale skewering vanity and self-importance: a pompous rocket convinced of his own greatness fizzles unseen in a ditch, a comedy of pride and self-delusion.

title: THE REPROOF AND REPLY
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic verse 'flower-thief's apology' for stealing garden flowers in church-time, playfully blaming the muses and the month of May. Themes: comedy, the garden, poetic fancy.

title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: Thirteen stories reviving Holmes after his apparent death, opening with 'The Empty House,' in which he reveals to a stunned Watson that he survived Reichenbach and unmasks Moriarty's remaining lieutenant, Colonel Sebastian Moran. The volume restores the detective to London practice through a fresh run of burglaries, blackmail, and murder.

title: The Return of the Heroes
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Harvest hymn celebrating the disbanding Union armies turning from war to the life-giving labor of the fertile American earth; nature, abundance, and the cost of war recalled.

title: THE RIME OF THE ANCIENT MARINER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A long supernatural ballad in which a mariner who kills an albatross suffers a spectral voyage of guilt, penance and reluctant redemption; themes of sin, guilt, the supernatural, providence and the sea.

title: The River of London
author: Belloc
summary: An essay-history of the Lower Thames as 'London River', framed by a firsthand voyage up the tide from the sea to the Pool that reads the past in successive stratified layers. Belloc contrasts the Thames with the Scheldt and Seine, attacks materialist history and the desolation wrought by modern industrialism, and mourns the Gothic London lost to the Great Fire, insisting London is a 'function of the Thames'.

title: The Road
author: Belloc
summary: A historical and theoretical essay (commissioned by a concrete engineering firm) on the road as a fundamental human institution. Belloc argues that roads should be consciously designed rather than left to haphazard growth, and traces the five great phases of the English road from the British trackway and Roman military road through the Dark Ages to the turnpikes, warning that a sixth transformation is now upon motor-age Britain.

title: The Romance of Tristan and Iseult
author: Belloc
summary: Belloc's English translation of Joseph Bedier's reconstruction of the medieval Tristan legend: the orphaned Tristan wins Iseult of the Golden Hair for his uncle King Mark, but the two drink a fatal love-philtre and are bound in an adulterous, doomed passion. The tale runs through flight to the forest, ordeal, exile, and their death together for love.

title: THE ROSE
author: Coleridge
summary: Anacreontic conceit in which a sleeping Cupid is found in a rose and set on Sara's breast; playful love lyric on the rose and the power of beauty.

title: The Rum Turn Tugger
author: Eliot
summary: Comic song-like portrait of the contrary curious cat who always wants the opposite of what he is offered; light verse on character.

title: The Runner
author: Whitman
summary: A four-line free-verse vignette of a lean, sinewy athlete in motion; an imagistic celebration of the healthy body and bodily energy.

title: THE SECOND BIRTH
author: Coleridge
summary: Short lyric epigram declaring that mutual love is a second birth from which life should be counted. Themes of romantic love and spiritual renewal.

title: The Selfish Giant
author: Wilde
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A Christian fairy-tale allegory of redemption: a giant's selfishness brings perpetual winter to his garden until he welcomes the children and the Christ-child leads him to Paradise.

title: The Servile State
author: Belloc
summary: A political-economy treatise arguing that industrial capitalism, being in unstable equilibrium, is drifting back toward legally enforced compulsory labour — a re-established slavery Belloc names the Servile State. Tracing the dissolution of pagan slavery by the Church, the medieval Distributive State, its wreck at the Reformation, and the failure of both socialist and 'practical' reform, he presents Distributism and Collectivism as the only alternatives. A foundational Distributist text.

title: The Ship Starting
author: Whitman
summary: Imagistic vignette of a ship setting out on the unbounded sea with all sails spread; the sea, the journey, voyage as the open road.

title: THE SIGH
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lyric tracing the recurring sigh for Mary through youth, woe and exile; love, melancholy, hope's decline and the wanderer far from home.

title: The Sign of the Four
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: Mary Morstan consults Holmes about her missing father and a mysterious annual gift of pearls, leading Holmes and Watson into a case rooted in a stolen Agra treasure, a pact of four convicts from the Andaman Islands, and a revenge-driven wooden-legged fugitive with a murderous pygmy accomplice. The novel introduces Holmes's cocaine habit and Watson's romance with Mary Morstan.

title: THE SILVER THIMBLE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: A playful occasional poem (voiced as by Sara) about a lost thimble, weaving the Arachne-Pallas myth and praise of the bard's verse; themes of poetry, classical myth, and gentle satire.

title: The Singer in the Prison
author: Whitman
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: A lady sings a redeeming hymn to convicts about the imprisoned soul freed by the pardoner death; music, sin, grace, the body, and death as deliverance.

title: The Sleeper
author: Poe
summary: A nocturnal lyric meditating on a beautiful dead (or deathly sleeping) woman, Irene, beneath the mystic moon; her sleep merges with the grave. Themes of death, the dead beloved, sleep and melancholy.

title: The Sleepers
author: Whitman
summary: Long dream-journey through the night in which the wandering soul merges with all sleepers and dreamers; death, night and sleep level and reconcile humanity.

title: THE SNOW-DROP
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric addressed to a snowdrop made immortal by Laura's (Mrs. Robinson's) song, bearing it to Pierian climes where the Phoenix nests and Lethe steals, a poem of art's immortality and memory.

title: The Sobbing of the Bells (Midnight, Sept. 19-20, 1881)
author: Whitman
summary: A brief free-verse elegy on the tolling bells announcing President Garfield's death and the nation's grief; themes of death, bells, the nation and mourning.

title: The Song of the Jellicles
author: Eliot
summary: Lilting song of the Jellicle Cats dancing by the light of the Jellicle Moon at the Jellicle Ball; joyful nocturnal dance verse.

title: The Song of the Wheels
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A militant ballad in which industrial machines stand silent in protest and the dispossessed workmen confront 'King Dives' in his iron garden. Themes: class conflict, the dehumanizing tyranny of the machine, and social revolt.

title: The Soul of Man under Socialism
author: Wilde
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Political-aesthetic essay arguing that abolishing private property frees a true Individualism, attacking poverty, charity, authority and public opinion, and championing the artist's autonomy from society.

title: The Speaker
author: Chesterton
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A literary-critical review of the letters and poems of the Manx poet T. E. Brown, meditating on friendship, the privacy of private letters, and frivolity as something sacred. Themes: friendship, the artist and his work, and reflection on death and judgment.

title: The Speckled Band
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: Doyle's own 1910 stage adaptation of his celebrated short story: an inquest into the terrified death of Violet Stonor opens the play, and Holmes and Watson must save her sister Enid from their menacing stepfather Dr. Rylott, whose greed for a dwindling inheritance has armed him with a deadly trained snake.

title: The Sphinx
author: Poe
summary: A short tale set during a cholera epidemic in which the narrator, sick with dread, mistakes a tiny death's-head moth on a windowpane for a monstrous distant apparition; a parable of misjudged proximity and the mind's terror. Themes of terror, omens, appearance vs reality.

title: The Sphinx
author: Wilde
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Wilde's decadent narrative poem in which a student addresses an immortal Egyptian Sphinx, conjuring her ancient lovers and exotic gods amid lust, decay and ruin, before recoiling toward his crucifix at the close.

title: The Sphinx Without a Secret
author: Wilde
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Short story of an enigmatic woman whose 'mystery' proves empty; a Sphinx without a secret, exploring appearance versus reality, secrecy and unrequited love.

title: The Star-Child
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy tale of a beautiful but proud and cruel foundling who, punished with ugliness for denying his beggar mother, undergoes a penitential quest of humility and charity, is restored, and redeemed in an explicitly Christ-toned arc of fall, suffering and redemption.

title: The Stark Munro Letters
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Domestic and Social Fiction · Romantic Love · Class
summary: In letters to an American friend, young doctor Stark Munro recounts his stormy partnership with the brilliant, unscrupulous, and bankrupt James Cullingworth, and his own struggle to establish an independent medical practice while wrestling openly with religious doubt and rationalist conviction. Semi-autobiographical, the novel traces Doyle's own early years as a struggling physician.

title: The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether
author: Poe
summary: A satirical horror-comedy: a visitor to a French madhouse discovers the lunatics have overthrown their keepers and taken over the asylum. Themes of madness, the world upside down, and appearance vs reality.

title: THE TAMING OF THE SHREW
author: Shakespeare
summary: Robust early Shakespearean comedy verging on farce: Petruccio woos and 'tames' the shrewish Katherine while disguised suitors compete for Bianca, framed by the Christopher Sly induction that explores persuasion, appearance vs reality, and the play-within-the-play.

title: THE TASTE OF THE TIMES
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram on the fashion for premature talent and child prodigies, punning on a 'petty Pitt'; satire of contemporary taste and celebrity.

title: THE TEARS OF A GRATEFUL PEOPLE
author: Coleridge
summary: A translated Hebrew dirge and hymn for the funeral of King George III, mourning a just king as a fallen day-star and praying for the royal line. Themes: grief and loss, kingship, faith, providence.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Poe
summary: A first-person tale of a mad narrator who murders an old man over his 'vulture eye', dismembers the body, then is undone by the imagined beating of the dead man's heart. Themes of madness, guilt, conscience and terror.

title: THE TEMPEST
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's late romance on the magician Prospero, exiled duke who raises a storm to bring his usurpers to his island, tests the lovers Ferdinand and Miranda, and finally forgives; central are magic and the supernatural, usurpation, forgiveness, nature versus civilization, and art.

title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
author: Bronte
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: Anne Bronte's 1848 novel, framed as Gilbert Markham's narrative enclosing Helen Graham's diary, in which a wife flees her dissolute, alcoholic and abusive husband Arthur Huntingdon to protect herself and her son; a morally bold social novel on marriage, debauchery, a woman's independence, faith and redemption.

title: The Terror of a Toy
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A satirical essay mocking the fad of banning toy bows and cannons, arguing that danger lies in the child not the implement and that the toy sword is 'the soul of the sword that will never be stained with blood'. Themes: satire of progressive faddism, common sense, and the poetry of arms and heroism.

title: The Thing
author: Chesterton
summary: A collection of apologetic essays defending Catholic orthodoxy ('Why I Am a Catholic') against scepticism, humanism, and the Protestant and modern drift. Themes: faith and the defence of dogma, conversion and orthodoxy, and critique of fashionable progress.

title: The Thousand-And-Second Tale of Scheherazade
author: Poe
summary: A satirical frame-tale extending the Arabian Nights: Scheherazade tells of Sindbad's encounters with modern marvels of science, which the incredulous king finds too improbable, and has her executed. Themes of truth stranger than fiction, satire and wonder.

title: THE THREE GRAVES
author: Coleridge
summary: A ballad-tale of a mother who, enamoured of her daughter's suitor, lays a curse that blights the marriage; a psychological study of jealousy, guilt and a mother's malediction; themes of jealousy, guilt and the supernatural.

title: THE THREE SORTS OF FRIENDS
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty epigram dividing friends into ac-, con- and in-quaintance (from his child's coinage) plus a fragment on inward beauty of womanhood; friendship and grace.

title: The Torch
author: Whitman
summary: Imagist miniature of Northwest fishermen spearing salmon by torchlight at night on a black lake; pure nocturnal image of fire on water.

title: THE TRAGEDY OF KING LEAR - THE FOLIO TEXT
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's great tragedy in blank verse on the aged King Lear who divides his kingdom by flattery, descends into madness and the storm, and is broken by filial ingratitude; central are kingship, the natural order, madness, suffering, and the question of justice in a pitiless world.

title: The Tragedy of the Korosko
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Gothic and Supernatural · Terror and Horror · The Unseen
summary: A party of European and American tourists cruising the Nile toward the Dervish frontier in 1895 is ambushed and force-marched into the desert by a Dervish raiding band. Their ordeal of captivity and threatened forced conversion becomes, in Doyle's telling, both an adventure narrative and a pointed defense of British imperial policy in Egypt and the Sudan.

title: The Truth of Masks
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Wilde's critical essay on Shakespeare's use of costume and illusion, arguing that archaeological accuracy is a method of artistic illusion and ending on the paradox that the truths of metaphysics are the truths of masks.

title: THE TWO FOUNTS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Stanzas to a suffering lady whose beauty dispenses only cheer; a dream-dwarf explains the two inner founts of Suffering and Cheer since Adam's sin. Themes: suffering, beauty, the fall, compassion.

title: THE TWO GENTLEMEN OF VERONA
author: Shakespeare
summary: Early Shakespearean romantic comedy in which the friends Valentine and Proteus both fall for Silvia; centres on the conflicting claims of love and friendship, fidelity vs betrayal, courtly love and disguise (Julia following Proteus dressed as a boy).

title: The Two Maps of Europe
author: Belloc
summary: A wartime handbook of six chapters from the winter of 1914-15, analysing the Great War as a contest between a German and an Allied re-drawing of Europe. Belloc surveys the true national groupings of the Continent by tradition, language and religion, arguing the war's stake is the preservation and extension of national liberties.

title: THE TWO NOBLE KINSMEN
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late tragicomic romance (with Fletcher) from Chaucer's Knight's Tale, in which kinsmen Palamon and Arcite, sworn friends, fall in love with Emilia and fight to the death for her; themes are the conflict of love and friendship, fortune's paradoxes, and chivalric ritual.

title: THE TWO ROUND SPACES ON THE TOMBSTONE
author: Coleridge
summary: A grotesque satirical ballad-lampoon in which the Devil and his grandam sit on a churchyard tombstone awaiting a buried 'Counsellor', a venomous personal attack steeped in diabolic and graveyard imagery.

title: The Unexpress’d
author: Whitman
summary: After all the world's poetry from Homer to Shakespeare, the poet wonders whether the best still remains unexpressed and lacking, a topos of inexpressibility.

title: The United States to Old World Critics
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: America answers European critics by pointing to its concrete daily building of a vast perpetual edifice rising to the stars.

title: The Unparalleled Adventures of one Hans Pfaall
author: Poe
summary: A proto-science-fiction hoax-tale: a bankrupt Rotterdam bellows-mender escapes his debts by ballooning to the Moon, narrated with pseudo-scientific detail. Themes of the quest, the journey, satire and wonder.

title: The Uses of Diversity
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1920 collection of light familiar essays on literature, society, religion and modern fads, defending wonder, paradox and orthodoxy against pseudo-scientific seriousness; satirical social criticism in the essay form.

title: The Valley of Fear
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Detective Fiction · Ratiocination Detection · Crime and Punishment
summary: The final Sherlock Holmes novel: a coded warning from Moriarty's informant Porlock leads Holmes and Watson to the murder of John Douglas at Birlstone House. A flashback second part reveals Douglas's past among the Scowrers, a murderous secret society in the Vermissa Valley coalfields of Pennsylvania.

title: The Valley of Unrest
author: Poe
summary: A short lyric on a once-peaceful dell, now restless and weeping over a nameless grave after its people went to the wars. Themes of death, mutability, melancholy and a haunted landscape.

title: The Village Street
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A melancholic narrative lyric: a nocturnal walk with a scornful maiden ends in parting and lifelong heartbreak, the once-pleasant elms now whispering mad, discordant melodies. Themes of lost love, melancholy and memory.

title: THE VIRGIN’S CRADLE-HYMN
author: Coleridge
summary: A short Latin cradle-hymn of the Virgin Mary singing the sleeping infant Jesus, copied from a Catholic print. Themes of divine love, the Virgin and childhood in hymn form.

title: THE VISIONARY HOPE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lyric of a sick man with no hope but one love-stricken visionary hope, sleep dreaded for its screams. Themes of despair, sickness, hope and love's despair as hope's ghost.

title: THE VISIT OF THE GODS: IMITATED FROM SCHILLER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A Bacchic ode after Schiller in which the Olympian gods descend on the poet, who drinks the nectar of inspiration that 'forbids me to die', a rapture of poetic immortality.

title: The Vital Message
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: A spiritualist apologetic written after the First World War, arguing that the war's suffering was meant to awaken humanity to psychic religion. Doyle sets out the case for survival after death, critiques Old Testament theology, and reviews mediums, seances, and scientific witnesses to spirit communication.

title: The Voice of the Rain
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: The rain answers the poet as the 'Poem of Earth', an eternal cycle of rising and returning likened to song.

title: The Wallabout Martyrs
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Elegy for Revolutionary War prison-ship dead, ranked above classical heroes as the foundation stones of America.

title: The Wanderings of a Spiritualist
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Spiritualism · Faith and Doubt · The Afterlife
summary: Doyle's travel memoir of his 1920-21 lecture tour to Australia and New Zealand to spread the spiritualist message, undertaken with his wife and children aboard the Naldera. Combines shipboard reflections on religion, empire, and the war with accounts of seances and psychic phenomena encountered en route.

title: THE WANDERINGS OF CAIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: Canto II of the prose-poem in which Cain, led by his innocent child Enos through a dark forest, cries out under relentless divine persecution and longs for death; themes of guilt, sin and the fall, and the outcast wanderer.

title: THE WANDERINGS OF CAIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A prose-poem fragment (prefatory note and plan) on the guilt-haunted, God-pursued wanderings of Cain after Abel's murder; themes of sin and the fall, guilt and the outcast wanderer, drawing on the Bible.

title: The War in South Africa: Its Cause and Conduct
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A 1902 polemical pamphlet defending British conduct in the Boer War against international accusations of atrocity, tracing the history of Anglo-Boer relations from the seventeenth century and answering charges over farm-burning and the concentration camps.

title: THE WASTE LAND  1922
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Waste Land (Sterility) · Greek Tragedy
summary: Title/epigraph page of Eliot's epoch-defining long poem (Sibyl epigraph, dedication to Pound); a fragmentary modernist epic of spiritual desolation, sterility and the ruined post-war city.

title: The White Company
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: Historical Novel · War and its Cost · Honour and Chivalry
summary: A historical adventure novel following young Alleyne Edricson as he leaves Beaulieu Abbey and joins Sir Nigel Loring's free company of archers during Edward the Black Prince's 1366-67 campaign in France and Spain, culminating in the Battle of Najera.

title: THE WILLS OF THE WISP
author: Coleridge
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: A Sapphic lyric in which deceiving will-o'-the-wisps that lure the traveller into the swamp are likened to a woman's perfidious glances; the supernatural and the femme fatale as deceiver.

title: The wind sprang up at four o’clock
author: Eliot
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lyric of wind breaking bells, swinging between life and death; the blackened river, death's other kingdom, Tartar horsemen; death and the uncanny.

title: THE WINTER’S TALE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late dramatic romance in which Leontes' irrational jealousy destroys his family, followed across sixteen years by pastoral renewal and the wondrous restoration of the lost daughter Perdita and the statue-like Hermione; its themes are jealousy, repentance, time, and redemptive grace.

title: The Wise Men
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: A Nativity lyric in which the three wise men, masters of all learning but truth, are humbled before the Christ-child; celebrates wonder, humility and the Incarnation over arid intellectualism.

title: The World below the Brine
author: Whitman
summary: A catalogue of the strange life of the ocean floor and its passions and wars, paralleling change between spheres of being; free-verse lyric on the sea, nature and metempsychosis.

title: The Wound Dresser: A Series of Letters Written from the Hospitals in Washington during the War of the Rebellion
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Whitman's Civil War letters and hospital memoranda from Washington DC, recording his nursing of wounded and dying soldiers and the human cost of the war. The text centers on death, suffering, comradeship, and the dignity of the common soldier, written in plain epistolary autobiographical prose.

title: The Wound-Dresser
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: An old man recalls tending the wounded and dying in army hospitals, dressing terrible wounds with impassive hand and burning heart; compassion, suffering and the human cost of war.

title: The Young King
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy-tale allegory in which a beauty-loving young king, taught by three dreams of the suffering behind his coronation finery, renounces luxury and is crowned by divine light as a Christ-like figure.

title: The Englishman
author: Chesterton
summary: A comic patriotic song invoking St George, English ale, beef and chivalry; nationalism, food and drink, the dragon-slaying hero.

title: The Appetite of Tyranny
author: Chesterton
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A 1915 polemical war essay arguing that Prussian militarism is a deliberate barbarism at war with civilisation; defends the Allied cause against tyranny in WWI.

title: The Crimes of England
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A 1916 satirical historical-polemical essay charging England's real crime as its long collusion with Prussia; an ironic patriotic critique tied to the First World War.

title: There Was a Child Went Forth
author: Whitman
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Catalog of a child becoming everything he beholds, from lilacs and farm animals to parents and the city; identity, childhood, perception, and the merging of self and world.

title: These I Singing in Spring
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Spring-walk poem of the 'poet of comrades' gathering natural tokens (the calamus-root) for lovers; nature, love, friendship and memory of the dead in free verse.

title: Thick-Sprinkled Bunting
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse apostrophe to the American flag prophesying its supremacy over the flags of kings; themes of patriotism, democracy and the flag of man.

title: This and That and the Other
author: Belloc
summary: A miscellany of Belloc's essays, sketches, histories and jests — from an ironic open letter to a young diplomatist and satires of pedants, spies and journalism, to reconstructions of Ethandune and the death of Robert the Strong, and lyrical evocations of England, France and Spain. The unifying air is Belloc's blend of wit, historical imagination and love of Christendom.

title: This Compost
author: Whitman
summary: Awe and terror at the earth's chemistry that grows sweet spring crops out of diseased corpses; death, decay, regeneration, nature, and resurrection of the grass.

title: This Dust Was Once the Man
author: Whitman
summary: Epitaph-quatrain for Lincoln, the gentle resolute man who saved the Union against the foulest crime in history; mortality, dust, and martyrdom.

title: THIS LIME-TREE BOWER MY PRISON
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse conversation poem in which the disabled poet imaginatively follows his friends through the landscape, discovering that nature never deserts the wise; themes of imagination, nature and friendship.

title: This Moment Yearning and Thoughtful
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet imagining brethren and lovers yearning in other lands; comradeship extended into international, cosmopolitan brotherhood.

title: Thou Art the Man
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A comic detective/ratiocination tale: the narrator unmasks 'Old Charley Goodfellow' as the murderer of his friend by springing the corpse from a wine-box to cry 'Thou art the man'. Themes of detection, guilt, deception and appearance vs reality.

title: Thou Mother with Thy Equal Brood
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Prophetic ode to America as the great Mother and ship of Democracy, blending body and soul, fusing past nations and pointing to a spiritual future Union.

title: Thou Orb Aloft Full-Dazzling
author: Whitman
summary: Invocation to the October noon sun as fructifying lover, asking it to shed its ray on the poet's chants and prepare his lengthening shadows and starry nights.

title: Thought
author: Whitman
summary: At a feast a spectral vision of a shipwreck at sea (the steamship Arctic) prompts the anguished question whether souls are drowned and matter alone triumphant.

title: Thought
author: Whitman
cluster: Vanitas · Contemptus Mundi · Vanity of Worldly Things
summary: Satiric meditation on people of high position whose attainments sink away, mocking false realities and rotten core happiness; vanitas, the self, and critique of society.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse catalogue on public opinion, the fall of corrupt officials and the rise of the democratic New World; themes of democracy and the common man.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A two-part free-verse meditation on America's birth-pangs, the war's price and the westward seeds of the future; themes of democracy, the West and transition through death.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
summary: A brief free-verse meditation on ownership, vista and the ever-continued journey toward what will yet be supplied; the open road, progress and the self.

title: THOUSAND HUMAN BEINGS, MEN, WOMEN, AND CHILDREN, MURDERED IN COLD BLOOD,
author: Coleridge
summary: Prose note and textual apparatus to the Ode to the Departing Year, condemning the Empress of Russia's atrocities and Britain's complicity in war, slavery and famine, citing the prophet Nahum.

title: Through the Magic Door
author: Conan Doyle
cluster: War and Empire · History · Nationalism and Patriotism
summary: A memoir-essay cataloguing the books on Doyle's own shelves, offering appreciations of Macaulay, Scott, and other favourite authors while musing on reading, creativity, and the fates of writers.

title: TIME, REAL AND IMAGINARY
author: Coleridge
summary: An allegory in which two children (a sighted sister, a blind brother) race endlessly on a faery mountain, figuring imaginary versus real time. Central themes: time, memory, the imagination.

title: TIMON OF ATHENS
author: Shakespeare
summary: A bitter, schematic tragedy/satire in which the lavishly generous Timon, abandoned by flattering friends once his wealth fails, turns misanthrope and curses humanity from the wilderness; themes of money, false friendship, ingratitude and misanthropy.

title: The Great Shipwreck as Analogy
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1912 essay reading the Titanic disaster as an analogy for modern civilisation and the State: overgrown, complacent, divided by class; meditation on death, courage and corporate conscience.

title: A Ballade of Theatricals
author: Chesterton
summary: A ballade written for a 1912 Titanic benefit, insisting that beneath theatrical illusion 'there are real things' — death, courage and human reality break through the unreal.

title: TITUS ANDRONICUS
author: Shakespeare
summary: Bloody Senecan revenge tragedy set in late Rome: the cycle of mutilation, rape and cannibalistic vengeance between Titus and Tamora. Central themes: revenge, the grotesque and horror, justice and barbarism.

title: TO * * * * * *
author: Keats
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Petrarchan-style sonnet of romantic longing in which the speaker, lacking knightly beauty, woos by spells and incantation; unrequited desire and fancy.

title: TO * * * *
author: Keats
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Lyric blazon praising a woman's beauty and imagining her as an enchantress in days of chivalry; romantic compliment fused with medieval fancy.

title: To --
author: Poe
summary: A short love lyric of dream-visions: the beloved's lips, melody and heart haunt the speaker's sleep, set against the worthlessness of gold. Themes of love, dreams and longing.

title: To --
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A brief love lyric in which the speaker, indifferent to his own desolate lot, is moved that the beloved should sorrow for a mere passer-by. Themes of love, melancholy and transience.

title: To a Certain Cantatrice
author: Whitman
summary: Gift reserved for a hero or rebel is bestowed instead on a singer; music and song, the cause of freedom, the rebel/common artist.

title: To a Certain Civilian
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A defiant address rejecting the civilian's wish for soft rhymes, affirming the poet's martial, war-born art and his role as singer of the funeral dirge.

title: TO A CHILD
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A light playful occasional verse addressed to a small girl ('Little Miss Fanny'); celebrates childhood, mirth and innocence in a brief comic lyric.

title: To a Common Prostitute
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Compassionate, scandalous address welcoming the prostitute as Nature welcomes all; the outcast, social injustice, the body, and radical acceptance.

title: TO A CRITIC
author: Coleridge
summary: A literary-satirical epigram retorting against a critic who quoted a passage out of context, threatening to pull out the critic's eye as 'analytic.'

title: To a Foil’d European Revolutionaire
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Consolation to a defeated revolutionary that Liberty waits latent and is the last to leave; revolution, martyrs, defeat made great, and undying liberty.

title: TO A FRIEND
author: Coleridge
summary: Blank-verse epistle to Charles Lamb tending his sick sister, and the poet recalling his own lost sister; friendship, grief, the sister, tenderness.

title: TO A FRIEND: (CHARLES LAMB) WHO HAD DECLARED HIS INTENTION OF WRITING NO MORE POETRY
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse epistle to Charles Lamb invoking classical Muses and Burns's neglected death to urge his friend not to abandon poetry; themes of friendship, vocation and the artist.

title: TO A FRIEND WHO SENT ME SOME ROSES
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet on a gift of roses whose fragrance whispers peace and friendliness; the rose as emblem of friendship and reconciliation in a nature setting.

title: To a Historian
author: Whitman
summary: Opposes the historian of surfaces with himself as chanter of personality projecting the history of the future; prophet-poet, identity, the common man.

title: TO A LADY WITH FALCONER’S SHIPWRECK
author: Coleridge
summary: A verse epistle accompanying the gift of Falconer's poem, evoking storm, shipwreck and the poet-as-shipwrecked-man, framed by gratitude and memory of absent friends. Themes: friendship, the sea, memory.

title: To a Locomotive in Winter
author: Whitman
summary: Ode addressing a locomotive in a snowstorm as fierce-throated beauty and emblem of modern motion and power, taking the machine as worthy of the Muse.

title: To a President
author: Whitman
summary: A terse rebuke to a president who has not learned the amplitude and impartiality of Nature; free-verse political epigram on the natural order, nation and reform.

title: TO A PRIMROSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric to the season's first pale primrose, emblem of timorous hope amid grief and the sweetness of joy following woe; themes of hope, the seasons, and consolation.

title: TO A PROUD PARENT
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram (after Lessing) implying a child's illegitimacy, since the mother will not teach the infant to call him 'father.'

title: To a Pupil
author: Whitman
summary: Exhortation that reform requires a magnetic Personality of clean body and soul; reform, the body, identity, and self-culture.

title: To a Stranger
author: Whitman
summary: Address to a passing stranger felt as a long-lost intimate; fleeting urban encounter, recognition, desire, the body and the dream of past shared life.

title: TO A VAIN YOUNG LADY
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty epigram chiding a beautiful woman for vanity, arguing that self-consciousness of her gifts impoverishes her charm; a satire of female pride and self-love.

title: TO A VIRTUOUS OECONOMIST: WERNICKE
author: Coleridge
summary: A complimentary epigram (after Wernicke) praising a frugal man who relieves the needy, hating poverty but not the poor.

title: TO A WELL-KNOWN MUSICAL CRITIC, REMARKABLE FOR HIS EARS STICKING THROUGH HIS HAIR
author: Coleridge
summary: A lampoon on a music critic with protruding ears, invoking the myth of King Midas's ass's ears to ridicule his bad judgment; personal satire drawing on Greek myth.

title: To a Western Boy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Address to a disciple ('eleve') warning that learning is useless without the blood and silent selection of lovers; comradeship, the body and discipleship.

title: TO A YOUNG ASS: ITS MOTHER BEING TETHERED NEAR IT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Sympathetic address to a foal of an oppressed race, hailing it 'Brother' and longing for a dell of peace and equality; animals, pity, social injustice, pantisocratic ideals.

title: TO A YOUNG FRIEND
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A blank-verse verse-epistle inviting a young friend to climb an allegorical 'Hill of Knowledge', celebrating retreat into nature, friendship and domestic calm away from worldly fame.

title: TO A YOUNG LADY
author: Coleridge
summary: A light occasional lyric rejoicing at a young lady's recovery from fever, half-jesting that Heaven has angels enough; themes of joy, illness and mortality skirted, with the spring and birds motifs.

title: To a Young Lady who Sent Me a Laurel Crown
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet exulting in the laurel crown sent by a lady, defiantly proclaiming poetic ambition above Caesars; the crown of poetic glory and fame.

title: TO A YOUNG LADY WITH A POEM ON THE FRENCH REVOLUTION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Verse epistle recalling youth and pity, then Freedom bursting her chains and the fall of the Tyrant in France, turning back to a lady and beauty; revolution, liberty, pity, love.

title: TO AN INFANT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A meditative lyric on an infant grasping for danger, made an emblem of fallen humanity clinging to Faith as nurse of souls; themes of innocence, faith, and human frailty.

title: TO AN UNFORTUNATE WOMAN AT THE THEATRE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A lyric addressing a 'fallen' woman seduced and forsaken, urging her toward penitent melancholy and recovered innocence; themes of seduction, the fallen woman and redemptive melancholy.

title: TO AN UNFORTUNATE WOMAN WHOM THE AUTHOR HAD KNOWN IN THE DAYS OF HER INNOCENCE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A short lyric figuring a ruined woman as a myrtle-leaf danced from its stalk by a flatterer and left to rot; an allegory of seduction, lost innocence and the fallen woman.

title: TO ASRA
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A love-sonnet to Asra (Sara Hutchinson) whose ever-welling love, likened to spring-waters through snow, the poet would transmute into a dower of happy life and eternity for her.

title: TO AUTUMN
author: Keats
summary: Ode to the season of ripeness and harvest that quietly accepts decline and the coming of death in its music of the soft-dying day; nature, the seasons, transience and serene acceptance of mortality.

title: TO BABY BATES
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A tender lullaby to an American infant contrasting wealthy Columbia with poor Britain yet affirming all are children of one God of Love; childhood, poverty, and divine love.

title: TO CAPTAIN FINDLAY
author: Coleridge
summary: A jaunty sea-toast saluting a ship's captain who rightly foretold a fair wind, with refrain 'Bravo! Captain Findlay'; conviviality and the sea voyage to Malta.

title: TO CHARLES COWDEN CLARKE
author: Keats
summary: Verse epistle of gratitude to his mentor Clarke for opening to him Spenser, Tasso and the classics; friendship, poetic apprenticeship and the passing of time.

title: TO DISAPPOINTMENT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: An ode banishing the fiend Disappointment and invoking sweet May to bring peace, health, and filial and maternal joy to the poet's mother in the Welsh vales.

title: To Dr. and Mrs. Field
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line note in which Dickinson acts with the leave of the bluebirds, whose approval she claims is required for anything they do.

title: To Dr. and Mrs. Field
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson sends a violet, apologizing that snowdrifts and a lost hat prevented her adding a stem and a butterfly.

title: To Dr. and Mrs. Field, 1884?
author: Dickinson
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: Dickinson thanks the Fields for flowers, saying they make the Expulsion from Eden indistinct, and jokes about a Beaconsfield remark on the gates to India.

title: To Dr. and Mrs. Field, 1885
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson sends the first flower of spring, noting the azaleas are still vivid while the frailer flowers have already faded.

title: To Dr. and Mrs. Field, 1885
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson apologizes for a delayed flower sent to the Fields.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter enclosing poems on homesickness and on friends blooming eternally in a changeless land.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter protesting a jointly-addressed letter, asserting the soul's solitude, and finding God present in Nature after seeing sunrise on the Alps.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A consolation note recalling how simple words comforted her at her own father's death and her mother's grief.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A consoling letter urging Mrs. Holland to live for others and affirming that death's sting is undone by resurrection.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A letter on the marriage of Mrs. Holland's daughter Annie, blending congratulation with mourning for her late father.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line note adapting a biblical phrase about loving one unseen.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A short poem asserting that truth is as old and eternal as God, and would perish only if God did.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A travel letter to the Hollands describing a journey through Washington and Philadelphia and a visit to George Washington's tomb at Mount Vernon.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: An editorial note describing the Dickinson family's return after fifteen years to the ancestral mansion where Emily was born and later died.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson writes to the Hollands about her family's move to a new house, her mother's illness, and how she misses their visits.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line postscript noting that the bobolinks have departed.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: An editor's note introducing a letter that reproaches the Hollands for not writing.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter relieved that Austin had seen Mrs. Holland alive, enclosing a poem on death arriving equally at any age.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line request that a flower be laid on the ailing Mrs. Holland's pillow.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter to the Hollands recounting a dream of gathering roses with them and describing fear stirred by a minister's sermon on death and judgment.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, 1857?
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter on the loneliness after the Hollands' visit, the death of a cat and of a young neighbor, and reflections on love and the power of death.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, 1859
author: Dickinson
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A note congratulating Mrs. Holland on the birth of a son, with prayers for the family.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, 1860
author: Dickinson
summary: A playful note about the Hollands' infant son nicknamed Byron, joking about the poet's clubfoot and genius and the impartiality of frost.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, 1864?
author: Dickinson
summary: A November letter mixing wry domestic news with grief over a dead child and a failing friend.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, 1883?
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter following the Hollands' travel to St. Augustine, on faded blossoms and enduring friendship.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, August, 1879
author: Dickinson
summary: A summer letter of domestic news followed by grief notes on Dr. Holland's death in October 1881.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Autumn, 1859
author: Dickinson
summary: An autumn letter about the coming cold, Vinnie's and relatives' illnesses, longing for the Hollands' visit, and the fragility of loved ones.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Christmas, 1881
author: Dickinson
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A Christmas letter to the widowed Mrs. Holland praising her self-forgetful grief and likening her to Emily Bronte.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Friday
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter complaining of unanswered mail, worrying over Mrs. Holland's health, and describing a bird singing unheard as an emblem of her own vocation to love.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Friday Evening
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter to Mrs. Holland accepting an invitation to visit Springfield by train, full of eager anticipation and warm remembrance.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, January 2d
author: Dickinson
summary: A very brief New Year's greeting wishing the sweetest New Year, merriest long life, and highest heaven.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Sabbath Night
author: Dickinson
summary: A Sabbath-night letter reflecting on a Bible verse about heaven, imagining her friends gathered there, and on flowers and friends that fade.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Saturday Eve
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter written amid illness and death—Austin's fever, a child's death, her buried garden—meditating on death as a leveler of proud and poor.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Saturday Eve
author: Dickinson
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A letter to Dr. Holland likening falling snow to descending swans, rejoicing that his child survived, and blessing their new home.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Spring, 1856?
author: Dickinson
summary: A short spring note describing her flowers, the wind and jays, and her affection for the few she loves.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Spring, 1878
author: Dickinson
summary: A spring letter alluding to Macbeth, on grief for the late Samuel Bowles and concern for Dr. Holland's failing eyes.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Thursday
author: Dickinson
summary: A letter of condolence to Mrs. Holland after her husband's death, offering the hope of heaven and asking gently about his final hours.

title: To Dr. J. G. Holland, and Mrs. Holland, Tuesday Evening
author: Dickinson
summary: A warm, playful letter to the Hollands mixing longing for their company with biblical allusions, newspaper reading, and thoughts of reunion in heaven.

title: TO EARL STANHOPE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A revised sonnet to Stanhope, casting him as an Abdiel-like faithful champion of Freedom and her God against rebellious nobility; themes of virtue, liberty, and martyred righteousness.

title: TO EDWARD IRVING
author: Coleridge
summary: Verses to the preacher Edward Irving on the divine Reason and Absolute Will, plus a comic Luther-on-devils squib; theological reflection mixed with affectionate wit.

title: To F--
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A love lyric: amid the woes of his earthly path the speaker finds solace in the memory of the beloved, likened to a serene enchanted isle in a stormy sea. Themes of love, consolation and melancholy.

title: TO FORTUNE
author: Coleridge
summary: Mock-serious ode addressing blindfold Fortune on buying a lottery ticket; gold, hope, poverty and the flower of hope. Satirical occasional lyric.

title: TO FORTUNE
author: Coleridge
summary: Brief prose epistle to the editor introducing the poem 'To Fortune'; a satiric/occasional note framing an address to the goddess Fortune and the lottery.

title: To Frances S. Osgood
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A short complimentary love lyric counselling the beloved to remain exactly as she is to be endlessly praised and loved. Themes of love, beauty and constancy.

title: To G. A. W
author: Keats
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Sonnet blazon praising the varied loveliness of a woman in her moods and graceful movement; romantic admiration of feminine beauty.

title: TO GEORGE FELTON MATHEW
author: Keats
summary: Verse epistle on the brotherhood of poets, lamenting the dark city that stifles the muse and longing for poetic fellowship and nature; friendship and the poet's vocation.

title: To Get the Final Lilt of Songs
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: To fully grasp the great poets one needs old age and the experience it brings as the final faculty.

title: To Haydon
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet to the painter Haydon, professing the poet's inadequacy before mighty art and praising Haydon's vision against the dull crowd; the artist, genius and aspiration.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A longer blank-verse love lyric recalling a single moonlit vision of Helen in an enchanted rose-garden, whose haunting eyes guide and enslave the speaker ever after. Themes of idealized love, beauty, eyes and memory.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Poe's classic lyric praising Helen's beauty as a Nicean bark bearing the wanderer home to 'the glory that was Greece, and the grandeur that was Rome'. Themes of beauty, idealized love and classical antiquity.

title: To Him That Was Crucified
author: Whitman
summary: Address to Christ as a fellow comrade and equal labourer transmitting the same charge across all lands and creeds; the Christ figure, comradeship, and universal brotherhood.

title: TO HOPE
author: Keats
summary: Personified ode to Hope as comforter against despondency and despair, ending in a patriotic prayer for England's liberty; melancholy answered by hope.

title: To Isadore
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A musical love lyric celebrating Isadore as a dream-enchantress whose voice and violet eyes wake old memories and turn the speaker's name to melody. Themes of idealized love, beauty, dreams and memory.

title: TO KOSCIUSKO
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet hymning the Polish patriot-hero Kosciusko, joining his name with Alfred's as everlasting heroic music; heroism, liberty and the immortality of great names.

title: TO LESBIA
author: Coleridge
summary: Imitation of Catullus's 'Vivamus mea Lesbia': carpe-diem invitation to love and count kisses, contrasting the recurring sun with humans' endless night of death.

title: TO LORD STANHOPE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A sonnet hailing Stanhope as an incorruptible 'Friend of Humankind' pleading the cause of Nature and Liberty; themes of patriotism, virtue, and freedom.

title: To Maggie Maher, Autumn, 1880
author: Dickinson
summary: A domestic letter to the absent servant Maggie Maher, describing the household's cats, an invalid hen, and the fading hollyhocks in her absence.

title: To Marie Louise (shew)
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A grateful blank-verse tribute to Marie Louise Shew, whose presence restores the despairing speaker's faith in Truth, Virtue and Humanity, her words echoing the divine 'Let there be light'. Themes of love, gratitude, faith and the angelic beloved.

title: TO MARY PRIDHAM
author: Coleridge
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A father's blessing on his son Derwent's betrothed, reviving the poet's hope at the fulfilment of a son's earliest wish in love. Themes: romantic/familial love, hope, fulfilment.

title: TO MATILDA BETHAM FROM A STRANGER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Verse-epistle praising a young poetess and urging bold yet truth-rooted art, linking female mind to music and to patriotic hope. Themes of art, nature, and the poet's vocation.

title: TO MISS BRUNTON
author: Coleridge
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Compliment to actress Miss Brunton via Thalia and the Tragic/Comic Muses; light lyric on the artist, beauty and the Muses of drama.

title: To Miss Eugenia Hall
author: Dickinson
summary: Note accompanying a wedding gift to Eugenia Hall, offering a smile to last a life if ripened in the sun.

title: To Miss Eugenia Hall
author: Dickinson
summary: Note thanking Eugenia Hall for carnations, praising her handiwork and remarking that loving robins and blossoms saves going to Heaven.

title: To Miss Eugenia Hall, 1885?
author: Dickinson
summary: One-line thanks to young cousin Eugenia Hall for flowers that, without lips, have language.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial note marking the birth of Samuel Bowles the Fifth.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Brief note describing flowers so beautiful they seemed dreamed until day and the flowers demurred.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial note describing sweet-peas gathered at dawn from Dickinson's garden and sent by train, with an accompanying line.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial description of Dickinson's flower garden through the seasons, and an introduction to the more sombre letters to Mr. Clark occasioned by successive deaths.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Dickinson tells Whitney that to relieve the irreparable degrades it, quoting Brabantio's resignation from Othello.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line message to Whitney that the crucifix requires no glove.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson sends flowers to the troubled-hearted Whitney, describing their intrusive sweetness as forgiven.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: A poem sent to Whitney about the dead as flitted seed, more remote than Heaven yet absolute as God, whom the soul goes to find.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: A four-line poem to Whitney stating that the vanished face is more distinct than the living, as capsules are for flowers.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson writes of unanswered prayer, Whitney's missed visit to the apple-blossoms, memory of her father and Bowles, and a sprained foot, closing with the vane defining the wind.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial note describing Dickinson's first letter to the son of the late Mr. Bowles, sent with pressed jasmine four years after the father's death.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial note on Dickinson's signature and her dream of the late Mr. Bowles, prefacing her congratulation on his son's engagement.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney
author: Dickinson
summary: Editorial note on the handwriting and uncertain dating of the first stanza Dickinson sent to Maria Whitney.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1877
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson thanks Whitney for her kindness in grievous days and reflects on the incomprehensible gift of mortality.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1878
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson writes to Whitney of the spirit within the body, the Northampton church bell, loss, and a rose likened to the singer Parepa.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1878
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson writes to Whitney of shared bereavement, hoping she is comforted, and reflects on Bowles's immortality.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1879
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson writes to Whitney that consciousness is our only home, offers to share her burden, and encloses a poem on wearing mortality lightly.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1882
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter enclosing a flower from a tree her father gave her, with a poem on immortality secreted in a star.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1882
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter regretting a missed visit, recalling the music of Whitney's late father's voice, and reflecting on peace and grandeur.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1882
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson confesses guilt over a note, mourns her vanished mother in an enclosed poem, and cites Paul on the weight of glory and the opened Heavens.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1883
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter thanking Whitney and approving her rest and Adirondacks trip, describing horses mowing hay for winter, rejecting the notion of disillusion, and recalling her mother's death.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1883?
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter asking whether Whitney's journey continues, discussing a picture of the actor Salvini as Othello, the arrival of autumn frost, and quoting Emily Bronte's verse on eternity.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, 1883?
author: Dickinson
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Dickinson likens the absent friend to a hidden bulb, praises the Biblical lily and Solomon, describes snow-hit apple-blossoms and birds, and reflects on the child Whitney tends.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, August 19, 1885
author: Dickinson
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Letter asking Whitney to address and forward a note to Mr. Jackson and admiring the sweet-peas she planted.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, August 2, 1882
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter recalling the late Mr. Bowles, recounting a servant's questions about the word genius, and celebrating his immortality.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, August, 1885
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter blessing Whitney upon her marriage and offering the writer's help and remembrance.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, October, 1883
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter of congratulation enclosing a short poem on a clock whose pendulum is wrecked by a sorcerer from Genesis.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, Probably 1884
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter about wanting to picture Whitney at her work in the city, describing Vinnie's garden of carnations and hyacinths, and reflecting on friendship, memory, and resurrection.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, Probably 1884
author: Dickinson
summary: Letter thanking Whitney for a gift of Ceylon tea and filberts, reflecting on honey, bees, temptation, and gratitude.

title: To Miss Maria Whitney, Tuesday
author: Dickinson
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Dickinson tells Whitney that her mother has died and that she feels Whitney present as they bear the body through the wilderness.

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague
author: Dickinson
summary: A note trusting that a dear friend is convalescing and that the lovely days are designed for it.

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague
author: Dickinson
summary: A note remarking that the Golden Rule is so lovely it needs no police to enforce it.

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague
author: Dickinson
summary: A note applying the biblical 'faithful in a few things' to commend a loyal cousin as a candidate for God's approval.

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line note thanking the Montagues for a gift 'delicate as bread of flowers.'

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague, 1881?
author: Dickinson
summary: A note wondering whom to thank for a gift of bread, comparing her delight to a robin's exultation toward a crumb.

title: To Mr. and Mrs. George Montague, 1881?
author: Dickinson
summary: A one-line note thanking the Montague cousins for a cake and 'the heart adjacent.'

title: To Mr. and Mrs. J. L. Jenkins, Mrs. Hanson Read, Mrs. W. A. Stearns, Mrs. Edward Tuckerman, Mrs. J. S. Cooper, Mrs. A. B. H. Davis, Mrs. H. F. Hills, Mrs. Jameson, Mr. F. F. Emerson, Maggie Maher, Mr. and Mrs. George Montague, Mrs. W. F. Stearns, Mr. J. K. Chickering, Mrs. Joseph Sweetser, Mr. Thomas, Niles, Mrs. Carmichael, Dr. and Mrs. Thomas P. Field, Mr. Theodore Holland, “H. H.,” Miss Eugenia Hall, Mrs. E. P. Crowell, and Mrs. J. C. Greenough
author: Dickinson
summary: Dickinson sends a child flowers and a butterfly verse praising the taxless, homeless freedom of the butterfly, and returns a rustic kiss.
